Title: Cardamom ad sparks clash between Bollywood star, India's food regulator
Article:
NEW DELHI: An advertisement for cardamom is at the centre of a legal spat between a Bollywood actor and India's most prominent food commissioner, with a court ruling set to shape how far companies can go in indirectly advertising brands whose promotion is restricted.
India restricts advertising for liquor and tobacco but officials have for years also frowned upon the use of indirect means, called surrogate advertising, by companies in such sectors promoting their brands in the guise of sodas, water or glassware.
While companies say these are genuine businesses in their own right whose advertising cannot be curbed, health officials say the advertisements are aimed at generating recall of the parent brand whose publicity is restricted.
Since 2024, India has been trying to finalise stringent guidelines to prohibit such advertisements outright.
In the case involving Bollywood stars, actor Ajay Devgn has sued the food authority of Maharashtra state, arguing he has been wrongly told to stop appearing in advertisements for Vimal cardamom packs, according to a non-public court filing dated Oct 15 reviewed by Reuters.
The state, whose food safety commissioner Tukaram Mundhe has become a national sensation for his aggressive stance on public health, asked Bollywood stars Devgn, Shah Rukh Khan and Tiger Shroff in August to stop appearing in advertisements promoting Vimal cardamom, arguing the brand is mostly known for its betel nut mix, or pan masala, which is banned in the state.
The spat in the High Court in Mumbai could set a precedent, New Delhi-based lawyer Anuj Tiwari said.
"The case will test both the fairness of the department's process before it imposes restrictions... and the parameters for deciding what counts as indirect advertising," he said.
In the advertisement available on Vimal Cardamom's YouTube page and posted two years ago, the Bollywood stars are seen celebrating, throwing saffron at each other after Devgn consumes the product.
The Hindi-language advertisement has 107 million views, while clips dubbed in other Indian languages have garnered millions more.
Devgn in his filing argues cardamom has not been prohibited in the state and "there is no bar in endorsing a product which is not prohibited."
Devgn did not respond to Reuters queries.
Mundhe told Reuters the state believes the advertisements are against public health interests, and the state is separately reviewing responses submitted by Khan and Shroff, although Reuters could not ascertain details of their submissions.
Dushyant Mahant, a lawyer for PB Agro, which holds the licence to make Vimal cardamom and pan masala, told Reuters the allegations were futile as the company does not promote Vimal in Maharashtra and only advertises the product via nationally televised broadcasts that cannot be restricted geographically.
Industry estimates show India's pan masala market was worth around US$5 billion last year.
Health experts say the product is a leading cause of oral fibrosis that often progresses to oral cancer.
While Maharashtra bans it, Vimal's tobacco-free pan masala sachets in other states cost around five rupees (5.4 US cents).
But they are often consumed with chewing tobacco, sold at kiosks as "twin packs" — a pan masala sachet alongside a tiny pouch of unbranded tobacco.
An adverse ruling in Devgn's case could affect Bollywood stars as endorsements can amount to up to 30 per cent of an actor's earnings, and promoting tobacco-linked products is more lucrative than other advertisements, said Suresh Mathew, a Mumbai-based screenwriter.
"Most actors know if a product is a surrogate for another product," he added.
"There are cases where certain actors have refused to lend their name to a product that they feel is harmful."

Title: India says 'cockroach' movement leader was told not to use passport
Article:
NEW DELHI: India's foreign ministry said on Wednesday that passport authorities asked 'cockroach' movement leader Saurav Das not to use his passport until he clarified information about his place of birth.
On Monday, Das said he was stopped at Delhi airport hours before he was due to fly to London to speak to students, after being issued the passport notice.
Das accused Prime Minister Narendra Modi's government of trying to silence dissent and stifle debate by blocking his travel to Britain.
Indian foreign ministry spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said passport authorities issue a notice if a discrepancy is noted or reported, amounting to a suppression of facts.
"He was also advised not to use the passport until he had submitted his response," Jaiswal told a regular media briefing, referring to Das.
Das has petitioned the Delhi High Court against the government move, legal news website LiveLaw reported. The plea will be heard on Thursday.
Das was among 14 people who scaled barricades on Oct 13 to enter the Jantar Mantar observatory in central Delhi, a day after it was removed from a list of designated protest sites.
He was detained for a few days.
Das led thousands of youth supporters demanding Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar's resignation over voter list revisions that critics say favour Modi's Bharatiya Janata Party.
This followed a weeks-long sit-in by supporters of the 'cockroach' movement earlier this year that forced Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan to resign over exam paper leaks.

Title: US proposes tariffs of up to 18pc on Malaysian goods in Section 301 probe
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The United States (US) has proposed tariffs of up to 18 per cent on Malaysian goods, citing concerns that the country's industrial policies and manufacturing practices contribute to excess production that undermines US commerce.
Malaysia is among 14 economies facing proposed tariffs under Section 301 of the Trade Act with proposed headline rates ranging from 15 to 35 per cent.
The other economies include China, Singapore, Indonesia, Thailand, Vietnam, Japan, and the European Union.
In a statement on Wednesday, US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer said investigations found that certain industrial strategies adopted by trading partners had created an uneven playing field for American manufacturers.
"For decades, many of our trading partners have adopted industrial strategies built on targeting manufacturing, wage and labour suppression, financial and other support, non-market economy inputs, and other market distorting practices that tilt the trade balance in their favour while eroding America's manufacturing base," he said.
USTR's findings against Malaysia centred on four areas, namely industrial and sectoral plans to expand manufacturing and exports, preferential financing through national funding programmes, insufficient action to address excess capacity linked to imports and foreign investments from non-market economies, and inadequate labour protections.
The report identified information and communications technology (ICT) and the automotive industry as sectors of particular concern, arguing that these policies could reduce commercial opportunities for US producers and exporters in Malaysia and other markets.
Under the proposed action, tariffs of up to 18 per cent would apply to Malaysian goods, on top of existing duties where applicable, but would be subject to exemptions for certain products.
On Malaysia, USTR said the proposed tariff rate of up to 18 per cent would be net of existing Section 301 tariffs, with exemptions for certain goods.
The proposal took into account existing duties under Sections 301 and 232, ongoing consultations with Malaysia, and commitments under the US-Malaysia Agreement on Reciprocal Trade.
However, USTR also proposed considering tariffs of up to 25 per cent, net of existing Section 301 tariffs, should it find that ongoing consultations and commitments under the reciprocal trade agreement were unsatisfactory.
Greer said the proposed action was intended to address what Washington viewed as unfair trade practices and strengthen the competitiveness of American manufacturers.
"In recognition of this, since 2016, leaders ranging from Donald Trump, to Joe Biden, to Xi Jinping, to Emmanuel Macron have recognised the threat that structural excess capacity and production poses for the global economy," he said.
Meanwhile, USTR acknowledged Malaysia's position that it operates a rule-based trade regime and does not contribute to structural excess capacity, with the government maintaining that its manufacturing ecosystem was critical to global and US supply chains.
Malaysia also argued that its economic model was market-based and responsive to global demand, while its exports were complementary to, rather than in competition with, US domestic production.
The investigation into Malaysia was initiated on March 11, with USTR holding bilateral consultations with the Malaysian government on May 12, although the discussions did not resolve Washington's concerns, according to the notice.
Interested parties have until Jan 5, 2027, to submit written comments and requests to participate in the public hearings, which are scheduled to begin on Jan 25, 2027, in Washington.

Title: Trump proposes new tariffs on imports from 14 trading partners, including Malaysia
Article:
WASHINGTON: United States (US) President Donald Trump's administration has proposed imposing new tariffs on imports from 14 trading partners, including the European Union (EU) and China, German Press Agency (dpa) reported.
US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer said tariffs on certain products from the EU would rise to 15 per cent.
Levies on Chinese goods would increase to as much as 20 per cent under the proposal, which also covers imports from India, Japan, Switzerland, Taiwan, Thailand, Vietnam, Bangladesh, Cambodia, Indonesia, South Korea, Malaysia and Singapore.
"For decades, many of our trading partners have adopted industrial strategies built on targeting manufacturing, wage and labour suppression, financial and other support, non-market economy inputs, and other market distorting practices that tilt the trade balance in their favour while eroding America's manufacturing base," Greer was quoted as saying in a statement.
Trump has imposed sweeping tariffs on the country's key trading partners since taking office in January 2025, arguing that the measures would boost US manufacturing and protect jobs.
However, the Supreme Court struck down most of the tariffs.
The latest proposal will be subject to hearings before a decision is made, with a US official saying the new tariffs were unlikely to take effect before January.
The move adds pressure on trading partners ahead of the G20 summit in Miami in December.

Title: NST Leader: Don't let anger drive us off the road
Article:
THERE are few things more infuriating than encountering inconsiderate and outrageous behaviour on the road.
A survey of 2,700 Malaysian respondents by Cilisos found that changing lanes without signalling, cutting into queues and hogging fast lanes were among the driving habits that annoyed motorists most.
Other pet peeves include double-parking without leaving a contact number, using a mobile phone while driving, misusing emergency lanes and refusing to give way. Such offenders may be cursed at or subjected to angry stares.
But do these offenders deserve to be attacked with a parang or meat cleaver, or punched by furious motorists in a fit of road rage? Certainly not. The consequences can be tragic.
An estimated 20 per cent of drivers fall into the high-anger category, exhibiting aggressive behaviour that can range from verbal abuse to physical violence.
Apart from perceived slights by other motorists, common triggers include traffic congestion, aggressive driving, poor road design, sudden lane changes and inconsistent speed limits. Poor traffic enforcement and everyday stress can also contribute to motorists' frustration.
Even the mild-mannered can turn aggressive behind the wheel. Psychological research suggests that the relative isolation of being inside a vehicle can make some drivers more reactive to perceived threats and provocations.
Few road rage incidents have been as deadly as the 2019 altercation at the Sungai Besi toll plaza.
Following a minor collision, motorist Syed Muhammad Danial Syed Shakir was struck by a car driven by Yew Wei Liang and later died. Yew was subsequently convicted of culpable homicide.
In December last year, the Federal Court reduced his prison sentence to 12 years.
More recently, a 62-year-old man was allegedly punched, elbowed and kicked following a collision involving his wife's car in Pasir Panjang, Terengganu, on Nov 23. Police arrested three men, aged between 39 and 44, who were remanded for four days on Nov 25 to assist investigations.
There are, however, ways to de-escalate such situations.
Above all, treat aggressive drivers as a hazard to avoid rather than a challenge. Never leave your vehicle during a confrontation.
Simple measures can help reduce the risk of road rage. Leave home before peak hours, signal clearly and well before changing lanes, and offer a brief hand wave or flash of your hazard lights as a courtesy.
Small courtesies can defuse tension. Avoid honking, flashing your headlights, making offensive gestures or glaring at  drivers.
Consider installing front and rear dashcams to record incidents and provide evidence in the event of confrontations. If another driver is tailgating or  braking suddenly, remain calm and allow the vehicle to pass when it is safe to do so. Change lanes only when conditions permit.
If an aggressive driver harasses you, head for the nearest police station or a well-lit, populated location such as a busy petrol station or highway rest area.
Call 999 if you are threatened or believe you are in immediate danger.

Title: Trump's Nvidia intervention rips up Wall Street playbook
Article:
INVESTORS were euphoric over Jensen Huang's return as chief executive officer of AI giant Nvidia on Monday.
But the extraordinary turn of events raises more questions than answers, particularly about the longer-term implications for Wall Street and the United States "free market".
Huang's return after only 11 days, which  President Donald Trump said would not have happened without his personal intervention, calls into question US corporate ethics, governance, trust and accountability, not to mention the supposed separation between Washington and Wall Street.
Huang returned after he resigned amid allegations of multiple extramarital affairs with subordinates and a suspected Chinese spy whose former employer, Singapore-based Mega-speed, was just blacklisted by the US government.
Only last week, Nvidia chairman Harvey Jones said the board would not reinstate Huang.
It's no surprise that the Trump administration sees Nvidia, and the AI financing solar system that revolves around it, as too big to fail.
Nvidia's plunging share price had wiped trillions of dollars from the US stock market, and the rout was threatening to snowball.
Trump was on record saying he wanted Huang back. Investors clearly agreed.
The Nasdaq leaped seven per cent after the announcement on Monday, the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index jumped 14 per cent, and Nvidia rocketed more than 30 per cent.
But Huang's sudden return is jaw-dropping.
Huang and Nvidia still face multiple investigations from US regulators, authorities and Congress into a wide range of issues, including the possible diversion of AI chips to China, suspected Chinese spying, accounting and financing questions, and antitrust concerns.
The White House's muddled approach also rings alarm bells.
On  Nov 15, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent told
Sunday Morning Futures
on Fox News that Nvidia was being looked into for a "culture of non-compliance" and needed to look "outside the company" for Huang's replacement.
A week later, when pressed on his previous comment, he told CBS's
Face the Nation
, "Well, Jensen is on the outside now."
Whether the White House's role in this saga is bullish or bearish depends on how you view the government's growing influence on private enterprises.
This isn't the Trump administration's first foray into the private sector.
It has bought a stake in chipmaker Intel, holds a golden share in US Steel, and has secured up to 15 per cent of revenue from certain chip sales made by Nvidia and Advanced Micro Devices in China.
But Huang's return is on another level.
Many investors may be shocked by what appears to be brazen political interference in one of the country's most important companies, and critics will say billionaire tech "gurus" are playing by a different set of rules than the rest of the country.
Or, no rules at all. How can this reflect "free and fair" markets?
Yet to others, Trump's intervention is akin to former European Central Bank president Mario Draghi's pledge at the height of the euro zone debt crisis in 2012 to do "whatever it takes" to save the euro.
The US government has signalled it will essentially do whatever it takes to backstop the tech industry and ensure the US beats China in the global AI arms race.
That, of course, calls into question the notion of efficient markets and the very definition of a risk asset, and raises the issue of "moral hazard".
Markets may have cheered the return of the 'outsider' but investors should be careful what they wish for. If the White House can help install someone as CEO, it can presumably remove them as well.
"Should we start pricing political risk premium into stocks seen as sensitive to the US government's interests?" says Shivaram Rajgopal, professor of accounting and auditing at Columbia Business School.
If share prices move more on shifts in political influence than on changes in corporate earnings, investors may have to fundamentally revise their investment principles and strategies for this new era.
Trump's unorthodox and often controversial policies have rewritten large parts of the rule book on which the global economic order of the last several decades has been based.
Maybe the Nvidia move is just the latest chapter, and investors will have to get used to more government involvement in markets, whether they like it or not.
The writer is from Reuters
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Can climate diplomacy build on COP31 collapse?
Article:
THE collapse of COP31 talks in Turkiye on Sunday without a political agreement left exhausted negotiators questioning the future of a process that for three decades has led the global fight against climate change.
For the small, vulnerable countries most exposed to rising sea levels and the increasingly extreme weather scientists link to rising carbon emissions, annual United Nations conferences are their chance to draw the world's attention to their plight and seek financial help.
But the failure of the Turkish talks, which follows on from weak outcomes at other COPs in recent years, lays bare the need for change.
Andres Martin Garrido Sanchez, director of environment in Peru's Foreign Affairs Ministry, said "the credibility of the process" was at stake".
"This system needs in-depth reforms," he said.
Simon Stiell, the UN climate chief representing the UN convention that underpins international climate talks, said the consensus-based system can still function, but work was needed.
"I have taken steps in engaging external knowledge leaders in advising on areas of potential reform. That is something I will be championing with considerable effort as we leave here," he said as the talks ended.
Two stand-out victories for UN climate diplomacy were the 1997 Kyoto Protocol, when the world for the first time agreed on legally binding targets to curb climate emissions and the 2015 Paris agreement, which established an aspiration to limit global warming to no more than 1.5°Celsius.
A major difference in Paris compared with Antalya was that the US was still engaged in the climate process in 2015.
The Antalya talks, the first since a UN report saying the world was set to breach the 1.5°C threshold that can prevent the worst consequences of warming, marked the second climate conference since US President Donald Trump withdrew from the UN climate process.
China, the world's biggest carbon emitter, but also a major part of the solution as a provider of low-carbon technology, has attended the talks but sought to be low profile.
James Fletcher, who led the CARICOM group of Caribbean nations in Antalya, cited the lack of a major power backing a positive outcome as a big issue.
"There isn't that one party that has sufficient gravitas that can get parties that may be far apart to come together," he said.
Delegates said, however, the need for a multilateral deal to direct the shift towards renewable energy has become less necessary as renewable energy becomes economically compelling.
China's clean energy exports last year alone, for example, will help the Global South avoid 257 million metric tonnes of carbon dioxide emissions per year once deployed — an amount equal to the emissions of France, according to analysis by Lauri Myllyvirta, co-founder of the ​Helsinki-based Centre for Research on Energy and Clean Air.
The business world as a result is less dependent on COPs to guide investment decisions.
"It used to be that you'd worry about how these (COP) decisions might affect the investment signal," said Chris Dodwell, co-head of the sustainability centre at Impax Asset Management.
"I don't think they really have that impact anymore…. economics have taken over and are driving the transition."
And bad as the absence of a deal was, some saw a hint of the positive in the wider refusal to accept a weak deal.
The determination of big oil
producers to block language on fossil fuel, arguably reflected the scale of progress that has been achieved.
Like-minded governments, meanwhile, have focused on smaller groups to get things done.  They have formed alliances to push together for faster emissions cuts and to rally finance, forestry initiatives, and efficiency programmes.
Such forums include the Conference on Transitioning Away from Fossil Fuels, or TAFF, the Green Grids Initiative, the Global Methane Pledge and the Beyond Oil and Gas Alliance.
"There is growing interest in how can we work together to move, not through consensus, but through a coalition of people that are willing to work together," said Maina Talia, climate minister of Tuvalu, which will next year host TAFF.
The writers are from Reuters

Title: 2,296 local firms generate RM29.89bil in actual, potential export sales – Miti
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A total of 2,296 local companies have received assistance through the government's export promotion programmes as of August, generating RM29.89 billion in actual and potential export sales.
Of the total, RM2.04 billion came from actual sales, while RM27.85 billion was in potential sales, according to the Investment, Trade and Industry Ministry.
The ministry said 310 participations in export promotion programmes for 2026 were approved by the Export Coordination Committee (JK-X), involving an allocation of RM116.85 million.
"Miti, through the Malaysia External Trade Development Corporation (Matrade) as the secretariat of JK-X, will continue to strengthen coordination among ministries and agencies through a whole-of-government approach in line with the 13th Malaysia Plan, the New Industrial Master Plan 2030 (NIMP 2030), the National Trade Blueprint and the National Science, Technology and Innovation Policy," the ministry said in a written parliamentary reply.
Miti was responding to a question from Datuk Ahmad Amzad Mohamed @ Hashim (PN-Kuala Terengganu) who asked on the implementation status of the "Made by Malaysia" agenda, particularly in developing high-technology products featuring designs, technologies and intellectual properties (IPs) owned by local companies.
He also asked how many local companies had successfully developed products with their own IP and the export value generated.
MITI said it provided the NIMP Industrial Development Fund (NIDF) as an enabling instrument to translate the NIMP 2030 mission into action at company level.
"Up to October, the implementation of projects under NIDF had benefitted 374 local small and medium enterprise (SME) and mid-tier companies across various industry sectors," it said.
On companies developing products with their own IPs, Miti said records from the Intellectual Property Corporation of Malaysia (MyIPO) showed that 48,548 IP registrations by local companies were recorded between 2021 and September 2026.
This figure comprised 45,801 trademark registrations, 1,444 patent registrations and 1,303 industrial design registrations.
"Patent registrations by local companies increased from 204 in 2021 to 318 in 2024, while industrial design registrations rose from 40 to 344 over the same period," the ministry said.
Between 2021 and 2025, a total of 667 overseas trademark registrations by local companies were also recorded, mainly in Indonesia, Thailand, Singapore, the Philippines and Vietnam, to protect their brands in overseas markets.

Title: KopMedia, AHMC partner Yapeim to strengthen infak programme
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Koperasi Media Prima Bhd (KopMedia) and AlHijrah Media Corporation (AHMC) have signed a memorandum of understanding (MoU) with Yayasan Pembangunan Ekonomi Islam Malaysia (Yapeim) to strengthen its continuous charitable giving initiatives through the Strategic Infak Partner Scheme.
Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Religious Affairs) Dr Zulkifli Hasan said the collaboration aimed to broaden public participation in sustained charitable giving through strategic partnerships, while strengthening the collection of infak funds to support Yapeim's programmes and initiatives.
"We are strengthening another effort with KopMedia, AHMC and Yapeim to empower communication and ensure our delivery system is more impactful and effective," he said at a press conference during the 2026 Yapeim Media Appreciation and Charity Night.
Also present were KopMedia chairman Mohd Fadzil Abdul Ghani and Yapeim Board of Trustees chairman Abdul Khudus Mohd Naaim.
The MoU was signed during the event.
In a related development, Zulkifli said Yapeim had channelled RM50,000 in cash aid to 50 media practitioners in need, with each recipient receiving RM1,000 to ease their financial burden.
He said the assistance was distributed in collaboration with five media associations and clubs: Kelab Media Putrajaya, Kelab Media KL dan Selangor, Malaysian Sportswriters Association, Selangor Photojournalists Association and KopMedia.
"Tonight, we are also celebrating media practitioners who have given Yapeim their support and provided extensive coverage. More than 100 media practitioners attended the event.
"Yapeim is moving in a positive direction, and we can see very good progress in its operations and business, including its education and welfare mandates," he said.
Zulkifli also encouraged the public to support Yapeim through contributions and infak via its various channels, enabling the foundation to carry out more economic development, education and community programmes to assist those in need.
"We can see the close relationship with the media. What we hope for is how Yapeim and the media can work together, contribute and share news and programmes by Yapeim that can be disseminated overseas.
"Yapeim has contributed significantly to welfare, education and business.
"This shows that Yapeim is becoming stronger, while at the same time requiring synergy between the foundation and media practitioners," he said.

Title: Anwar: Food security needs more than bigger harvests
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Strengthening Malaysia's food security will require more than higher production, with Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim calling for longstanding weaknesses in agriculture, livestock and fisheries to be addressed.
He said businesses with strong potential should have better access to early financing, including through Agrobank, to help them expand domestic food production and build sustainable operations.
Citing Farm Fresh Bhd as an example, Anwar said the company's growth had been supported by initial capital from Khazanah Nasional Bhd, demonstrating how early assistance could help promising businesses develop and reach wider markets.
He was responding to a question from Farm Fresh group chief operating officer Azmi Zainal on how the government could protect consumers while ensuring food producers remained viable amid rising costs.
Speaking on RTM's special Di Sebalik Keputusan... Dialog Negara programme last night, Anwar said geopolitical tensions, including conflicts involving Iran, Israel and the United States, as well as the Russia-Ukraine war, had added pressure to food and agriculture industries.
Shipping costs had risen tenfold, pushing up the price of imported inputs such as phosphates transported through strategic routes, including the Strait of Hormuz.
"All countries in Asia and even in Europe are now facing political and social tensions due to rising prices of goods, partly due to national fiscal policies and partly due to the problem of rising imported goods," he said.
Anwar, who is also Finance Minister, said efforts to boost domestic production must be matched by reliable supplies of essential inputs, including fertilisers, and better marketing infrastructure.
He also warned that large government allocations would achieve little without strict oversight to prevent leakages and the entrenched practice of paying commissions.
"Governance must not be neglected, as excessive leakages of funds can lead to a situation where the problem becomes deeply systemic. When we eventually take action, the backlash is severe and the anger widespread because those involved have become accustomed to receiving commissions," he said. — BERNAMA

Title: No eligible flood victims will miss out on RM1,000 aid, says Zahid
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: All eligible flood victims will receive the RM1,000 compassionate cash aid, including those who do not seek shelter at temporary relief centres, Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said.
He said the government had a mechanism to ensure that victims who chose not to evacuate to centres also receive the assistance, subject to verification.
"Some may have their own reasons for not moving to relief centres, such as staying at their children's or siblings' homes.
"We have a mechanism in place requiring them to lodge a police report to verify that they are flood victims," he told Bernama.
Zahid, who is also Central Disaster Management Committee chairman, was speaking after attending the 14th Asean Ministerial Meeting on Disaster Management (AMMDM), the 15th Conference of the Parties (COP) to the Asean Agreement on Disaster Management and Emergency Response (AADMER), and related meetings hosted by Indonesia.
He is on a five-day working visit to Indonesia and arrived in Jakarta yesterday after holding several meetings on rural development cooperation in Bali since Monday.
The aid provides RM1,000 to each eligible head of household.
On Nov 19,  Zahid told the Dewan Rakyat that priority was given to flood victims staying at relief centres, while those who did not evacuate were also eligible if registered at a flood victim registration centre.
On the allocation for the aid, he said the amount would depend on current needs, but cautioned the public against abusing the assistance mechanism.
"Do not take advantage of a difficult situation. I am confident that Nadma (National Disaster Management Agency) handled this as best as possible," he said.
Apart from financial assistance, Zahid said the government was also strengthening flood preparedness, with Nadma having deployed the necessary assets to states affected by floods.
Preparations were also under way in other states at risk.
He said disaster management efforts were being coordinated through a whole-of-government approach, regardless of political differences.
"We are colour-blind when it comes to managing disasters," he said, adding that coordination was carried out through the Central Disaster Management Committee, with Nadma serving as its secretariat.
Zahid also thanked more than 580 non-governmental organisations (NGOs) involved in the current disaster management efforts and hoped that all preparations could be implemented in a more coordinated manner.
Ahead of the northeast monsoon, he had previously said that more than 100,000 personnel from various response and technical agencies were mobilised, supported by nearly 2,500 boats, more than 2,000 four-wheel-drive vehicles, over 1,100 lorries and 28 aircraft.
As of this morning, 1,181 flood victims from 333 families were still taking shelter at 10 relief centres in Selangor, Perak and Terengganu, with 819, 211 and 151 victims respectively, Bernama reported.
Sabah was also affected by floods following heavy rain since yesterday. The Sabah Disaster Management Committee said 153 residents from 42 families in three villages in the Sook district had been evacuated to a relief centre as of noon today.

Title: Anwar backs adding mental health to school curriculum
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has backed the Ministry of Education's (MOE) proposal to teach mental health in schools to help pupils cope with stress.
He said the lessons should be handled sensitively and taught in a way that engages pupils.
Speaking on RTM's Dialog Negara programme on TV1 tonight, Anwar said religious and moral education should also help pupils put what they learn into practice.
"Religious and moral education should be central. Islamic education should make a difference too. Muslim pupils study Islam and pray together, but I agree that what they learn does not always translate into how they live," he said.
Anwar said schools needed more trained counsellors to deal with serious cases. Expanding counselling services would require substantial funding and could take time, he said, calling for greater public awareness in the meantime.
"Our responses are very compartmentalised. We need to raise awareness in the community. Parents have responsibilities, and so do teachers. If we take those responsibilities seriously and do our best, we can address some of these problems," he said.
Citing a briefing to the Cabinet, Anwar said most cases involving school pupils, including bullying, stemmed from pressures at home, such as excessive academic demands, as well as mistreatment and abuse at school.
He said the government could consider proposals from the Education and Health ministries and non-governmental organisations, but he also called for wider awareness, particularly among families.
"However busy parents are, they still have a responsibility to care for and guide their children, give them time and space, and show them affection," he said.
The programme aired on TV1 and was simulcast on Bernama TV, Astro AWANI, TV3, TV AlHijrah and TVS.
The panellists included Komuniti Pejuang Hartanah founder Datuk Ahyat Ishak, KRA group strategy director Amir Fareed Rahim, medical officer and social media influencer Dr Malar Santhi Santherasegapan, and entrepreneur and digital content creator Adam Shamil.
The panel also included PlusVibes Group founder and chief executive Dr Madiha Fuad, Farm Fresh Berhad group chief operating officer Azmi Zainal, independent preacher Izzhar Nazri, Architects of Diversity (AOD) Malaysia founder Jason Wee, and Universiti Teknologi MARA (UiTM) Student Representative Council president Mohamad Adib Hazim Mohamad Razali. -- BERNAMA
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Anwar urges doctors, teachers to accept rural postings [WATCH]
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has urged doctors, teachers and other civil servants to accept postings in rural and remote areas, saying personal preferences should not leave communities without essential services.
He said the government was willing to adjust postings where reasonable, with access to healthcare in remote communities remaining a priority.
"There are difficulties with postings. Where we can make adjustments, we will.
"But if everyone gets to choose, who will choose to work as a doctor in Kapit in Sarawak, or in Gua Musang or Ulu Kelantan?" he said on RTM's Dialog Negara programme on TV1 tonight.
The programme was also simulcast on Bernama TV, Astro AWANI, TV3, TV AlHijrah and TVS.
Anwar said the same staffing challenges applied to engineers and teachers.
Postings across the public sector were needed to keep government services running in remote parts of Sabah, Sarawak and Peninsular Malaysia, he said.
The programme's panellists included Komuniti Pejuang Hartanah founder Datuk Ahyat Ishak, KRA group strategy director Amir Fareed Rahim, medical officer and social media influencer Dr Malar Santhi Santherasegapan, and entrepreneur and digital content creator Adam Shamil.

Title: Libyan student charged with reckless driving that killed retired soldier
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A 32-year-old Libyan student pleaded not guilty in the magistrate's court today to a charge of reckless driving that caused the death of a retired soldier on Jalan Jelatek last Saturday.
Ali Abdul Rahman Mahmoud Elmaki, a private university student, entered his plea after the charge was read out in english before magistrate Amalina Johar.
He was accused of driving a Proton Saga recklessly and dangerously along Jalan Jelatek, from Wangsa Maju towards Taman Keramat, at 1am on Nov 21, resulting in the death of 43-year-old Mohd Hairezam Omar.
The charge was framed under Section 41(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987, which carries a maximum fine of RM50,000 or imprisonment of up to 10 years upon conviction. A conviction under the section also carries an endorsement on the offender's driving licence.
Deputy Public Prosecutor Mohamad Fadhly Mohd Zamry objected to bail, citing the seriousness of the offence and the accused's status as a foreign national.
However, he said that should the court exercise its discretion to grant bail under Section 388 of the Criminal Procedure Code, the prosecution proposed RM70,000 bail with two Malaysian sureties.
"The prosecution also requests additional conditions: that the accused's passport be surrendered to the court, that he reports to the nearest police station at least once a month, and that he is prohibited from using his driving license until the conclusion of the case.
"I request that the court consider these conditions should bail be granted, given that the accused is a foreign national and poses a flight risk," he said.
Lawyer  K. Ramalingam, representing the accused, requested bail of about RM10,000, saying his client was pursuing a master's degree and was scheduled to sit for examinations next month.
"The accused resides in Malaysia with his wife and has a permanent address on Jalan Ampang. He is also prepared to accept all additional conditions requested by the prosecution," he said.
The court granted bail at RM17,000 with two Malaysian sureties, subject to the accused surrendering his passport, reporting to a nearby police station once a month and having his driving licence suspended until the conclusion of the case.
The court has set Jan 28 for the next mention of the case.
It was reported that the victim was riding his motorcycle from Taman Keramat towards Setiawangsa when a car driven by the Libyan allegedly ran a red light and hit him.
The victim suffered severe injuries and was pronounced dead at the scene.
Alcohol and urine screening tests conducted on the driver returned negative.

Title: Govt exploring establishment of AI wealth fund for Malaysians - Anwar
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The government will study whether to set up a fund to share the economic gains from artificial intelligence (AI) with Malaysians, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said tonight.
Anwar said he had asked the Communications and Digital ministries to study the options, including a proposal by US Senator Bernie Sanders for legislation to establish an AI fund that would pay dividends to Americans.
"I agree in principle. We can start engaging now, even before legislation is in place. For example, when we set a minimum wage, multinational companies have to comply too.
"At first, they objected, saying they came to Malaysia because wages were low. That may have been true 30 years ago. They now have to accept that living standards have risen," he said on RTM's Dialog Negara programme on TV1 tonight.
The programme was also simulcast on Bernama TV, Astro AWANI, TV3, TV AlHijrah and TVS.
Anwar said Malaysia imposed firm conditions on foreign AI investors, including requirements to provide water supply infrastructure and train Malaysians in advanced AI skills.
The Prime Minister cited what he described as a USD15 billion investment by Google.
He said the conditions included spending RM600 million on water supply infrastructure in Negeri Sembilan and providing advanced AI training for 1,000 young Malaysians, with Universiti Malaya as an example of a potential training partner.
"If the conditions are too onerous, investors may stay away. We should make clear that we welcome investment while taking firm steps to keep inequality from widening," he said.
Anwar said governments had a role in ensuring the benefits of growth were more widely shared across the economy.
The spread of AI made that more urgent because it could deepen inequality, he said.
On the impact of AI on jobs, Anwar said rapid technological change and unexpected shocks could bring challenges, including financial pressures. He said people could anticipate those problems and devise solutions.
He said government departments and the private sector should receive support to create new jobs as technology evolves.
The Dialog Negara panellists included Komuniti Pejuang Hartanah founder Datuk Ahyat Ishak, KRA group strategy director Amir Fareed Rahim, medical officer and social media influencer Dr Malar Santhi Santherasegapan, and entrepreneur and digital content creator Adam Shamil.

Title: Urban Renewal Bill will protect residents' rights, says Anwar
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has given assurance that the proposed Urban Renewal (URA) Bill would protect existing residents' rights, including those who oppose redevelopment, even as the government lowers the consent threshold from 100 per cent to between 70 and 80 per cent.
Anwar said the Bill was needed to allow run-down housing, particularly in Kuala Lumpur, to be redeveloped, and requiring every resident to agree had made it difficult for projects to proceed.
"If you require 100 per cent consent, these housing projects won't go ahead. We decided on a threshold of 70 or 80 per cent, with guarantees to protect the rights of those who disagree.
"I can't bear to see housing in such poor condition in Kuala Lumpur. Something has to be done, and we need a law with clear guarantees that protect the rights of existing residents," he said on Dialog Negara programme on TV1 tonight.
The programme was also simulcast on Bernama TV, Astro AWANI, TV3, TV AlHijrah and TVS.
Anwar said the government was developing several new sites in Kuala Lumpur and other major cities under its Madani development initiative.
He expected to launch several housing projects this December or January next year, adding that such developments typically took two to three years and that work already under way was nearing completion.
He said the new homes would be considerably more comfortable and that developers would have to meet conditions set by local authorities before any agreement was signed.
Strict enforcement was needed to reassure residents after past projects had been left unfinished for years without firm action, he said.
Anwar also rejected claims that the Bill was intended to help a particular ethnic group take control of residential areas or to serve developers' interests. He said the MADANI government remained committed to safeguarding the interests of Malays and Bumiputera.
"For the first time since independence, land in Kuala Lumpur has been designated as Malay reserve land, with 50 acres to start with. That has never happened before. We will not give in to demands from powerful investors," he said.
The Dialog Negara panellists included Komuniti Pejuang Hartanah founder Datuk Ahyat Ishak, KRA group strategy director Amir Fareed Rahim, medical officer and social media influencer Dr Malar Santhi Santherasegapan, and entrepreneur and digital content creator Adam Shamil.

Title: Teen mum charged with stabbing newborn to death, boyfriend admits concealing birth
Article:
TAIPING: A 19-year-old teenager was brought before the magistrate's court today on a charge of murdering her newborn baby girl by stabbing last week.
Nurul Iman Najiha Abdullah nodded when the murder charge was read out before magistrate R. Prabakaran.
However, no plea was recorded as the case falls under the jurisdiction of the High Court.
She was accused of murdering her biological daughter in an oil palm area behind a house in Kampung Panchor, Pantai Remis, in the Larut, Matang and Selama district, between Nov 14 and 16.
The charge was framed under Section 302 of the Penal Code, which carries the death penalty or imprisonment of between 30 and 40 years.
If not sentenced to death, an offender is also liable to whipping of at least 12 strokes upon conviction.
In a separate charge, Iman Najiha and her boyfriend, Mohamad Aidil Eikmal, also 19, were jointly charged with concealing the birth of the baby girl by secretly burying her body at the same location during the same period.
They were charged under Section 318 of the Penal Code, read together with Section 34 of the same code, which provides for a maximum prison sentence of two years, or a fine, or both, upon conviction.
Aidil pleaded guilty, while Iman Najiha claimed trial.
Deputy Public Prosecutor Farihah Adilah Faizal requested bail of RM50,000 with one surety for each accused. No bail was offered for the murder charge faced by Iman Najiha.
However, National Legal Aid Foundation counsel Nurul Hanis Mohd Zaini, representing both accused, appealed for lower bail, saying this was their first offence and that they worked as an eatery assistant and construction labourer respectively.
"Iman Najiha also has mental health issues but has never sought treatment," the lawyer said.
Bail was set at RM5,000 with two sureties for each accused.
The court fixed Jan 4 for a re-mention, for Iman Najiha to appoint a lawyer and for the Social Welfare Department to submit a social report on Aidil ahead of sentencing.
On Nov 19, Perak Police Chief Datuk Mohd Alwi Zainal Abidin said a newborn baby girl had died after allegedly being stabbed by her biological mother in Pantai Remis on Nov 14.
He said preliminary investigations found that the 19-year-old had committed the act at her home before contacting her boyfriend to help bury the baby's body behind the house.

Title: Act 173, Act 172 to be amended to give UiTM students more freedom to speak out
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The government will amend provisions in two laws to give Universiti Teknologi MARA (UiTM) students more freedom to speak out, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said tonight.
He said the changes to the Universiti Teknologi MARA Act 1976 (Act 173) and the Educational Institutions (Discipline) Act 1976 (Act 174) would run alongside efforts to repeal certain provisions of the Universities and University Colleges Act 1971 (AUKU) and introduce a new legal framework for higher education.
Speaking on RTM's Dialog Negara programme tonight, Anwar said a broader overhaul of university laws would take time, but steps to expand student rights should move ahead, including for UiTM students covered by Acts 173 and 174.
"I've already said that my directive should apply across the board. That means action must be taken even if the planned amendments take longer," he said, adding that the Higher Education Ministry was moving quickly to repeal provisions in AUKU.
Anwar said some provisions in the two laws governing UiTM students imposed tighter restrictions and should be reviewed to give students more room to express their views and think independently.
"Our Bumiputera students should be given space and freedom. Let them speak. Let them express their views. Why should we restrict how they think?" he said.
He said discipline had long been used to justify restrictions on student expression, but, in this modern era, universities should trust students to exercise their judgement and give them opportunities to develop it.
"I don't want to use the law to police students. Let's give them room. If we don't help young people develop their judgement and show confidence and trust in them, what kind of future will we have?" he said.
Anwar said he believes university students were mature enough to express their views and discuss current affairs and politics.
However, he added, students who committed criminal offences would remain subject to the relevant laws. -- BERNAMA

Title: Corruption in Malaysia is systemic, requires firm action - Anwar [WATCH]
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has described corruption in the country as a systemic issue that requires the sustained commitment and firm resolve of all parties to eradicate it, including by fostering an awareness of integrity among the younger generation.
He noted that the fight against corruption is no easy task, given that the practice has become deeply entrenched within the system.
Therefore, he said the government must continue to take decisive action, without allowing the pursuit of popularity to be a primary consideration.
"Corruption in this country has become systemic. That is what I inherited. We have to stand firm and keep going, whether it's popular or not. Popularity is secondary," he said on RTM's Dialog Negara programme on TV1 tonight, which was also simulcast on RTMKlik, Bernama TV, Astro AWANI, TV3, TV AlHijrah and TVS.
Anwar said fighting corruption had proved harder than expected, making it all the more important to instil a sense of integrity from an early age, as young people could drive change and help secure Malaysia's future.
He said he had reached out to young people through various programmes, including meetings at higher education institutions, to encourage them to make integrity a guiding principle.
"We want them to hold on to their ideals. They are our hope. If we can convince Gen Z and Gen Y of the importance of integrity, our future will be more secure. That is my hope," he said.
Asked about allegations that influential people linked to corruption received preferential treatment, Anwar said the rule of law must be upheld, and the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) must be free to investigate without interference from interested parties.
He cited the case of his former senior political secretary, Datuk Seri Shamsul Iskandar Mohd Akin, who was charged in a corruption case. Anwar said he had stayed out of the investigation.
"When someone close to me is being investigated, of course I ask what it's about. He told me, and I said I wouldn't interfere. He was then charged. Has anything like that happened before? No. My Cabinet colleagues know I won't defend anyone involved in corruption," he said.
Looking ahead to 2027, Anwar said he hoped all Malaysians would carry out their responsibilities with integrity so that the country's development continued to be guided by that principle.
He said students, families and the wider community all had a part in building the country, alongside leaders and civil servants.
"Our problems are about principles and conduct. We shouldn't hate one another or see these problems through the lens of race. We have to put things right together and build on our strengths. As I've said, we have tremendous potential to raise Malaysia's standing," he said.
The Dialog Negara panellists included Komuniti Pejuang Hartanah founder Datuk Ahyat Ishak, KRA group strategy director Amir Fareed Rahim, medical officer and social media influencer Dr Malar Santhi Santherasegapan, and entrepreneur and digital content creator Adam Shamil.
The panel also included PlusVibes Group founder and chief executive Dr Madiha Fuad, Farm Fresh Berhad group chief operating officer Azmi Zainal, independent preacher Izzhar Nazri, Architects of Diversity (AOD) Malaysia founder Jason Wee, and Universiti Teknologi MARA (UiTM) Student Representative Council president Mohamad Adib Hazim Mohamad Razali. -- BERNAMA

Title: Govt mulls tighter regulations to control influx of foreign e-commerce products [WATCH]
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The government will consider introducing stricter regulations to control the entry of cheap goods through international e-commerce platforms, especially from China, said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.
Anwar, who is also the Minister of Finance, said the influx of foreign products affects the macro economy and directly undermines the competitiveness of local entrepreneurs.
"I agree, and I think we should introduce stricter regulations," he said on Radio Televisyen Malaysia's (RTM) special "Di Sebalik Keputusan..." Dialog Negara programme aired tonight.
The prime minister responded to Chunk & Dunk's founder, Adam Shamil, on how the government balances competition from cheap international e-commerce goods on platforms such as Pinduoduo and Temu to protect local entrepreneurs and brands.
However, Anwar said the government will not completely block or restrict these foreign platforms, but the quality and standards of the products sold must be monitored, including their halal status.
"This is why we are starting to impose some restrictions now. We will give them the opportunity to enter on the condition that local companies are involved or that they provide guarantees of quality and health. And, if it is labelled halal, it must be guaranteed as halal," he said.
Anwar said the matter was also raised with China's leaders during several visits to the country, and Chinese President Xi Jinping informed of China's readiness to increase space for Malaysian export goods.
"We do not intend to restrict, but what we want is investment and trade, not an influx of cheap goods... and this is killing smaller companies.
"So, we have agreed in the Cabinet to take several steps to curb slightly, but not completely restrict, because this goes against our (trade) policy to allow increased imports," he said.
At the same time, Anwar also reminded the people not to be mesmerised by advertisements for products whose quality has not been guaranteed.
"This is an old theory, Babylon's conspicuous consumption. Sometimes, people want to purchase unnecessary things because of extensive advertising," he said.
Anwar said the government needs to monitor advertisements, ensure product quality, and strengthen consumer education so people buy what they need and do not spend more than they earn. -- BERNAMA

Title: GE16 must be held before February 2028 [WATCH]
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The 16th General Election (GE16) must be held before February 2028, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, suggesting it could take place before or after National Day next year.
"GE16 must be held before February 2028; that is the rough timeframe. So, please be patient... It will likely be either before or after National Day. It won't be beyond that," he said during the RTM's Dialog Negara: Di Sebalik Keputusan (National Dialogue: Behind the Decisions) programme on TV1 tonight.
Asked what a new mandate would mean for his administration, Anwar said the make-up of the next government would depend on the support voters gave each party.
If given the opportunity, he said, of course, he wanted to continue leading the country.
"I love this country. I believe in what it can do. I have high hopes for our young people, and I want Malaysia to stand tall as a strong nation in the region and the world," he said.
Separately, Anwar urged Malaysians to scrutinise religious claims and check the evidence behind them, including when those claims come from political leaders like himself.
He said religious outreach must be grounded in knowledge and warned that people could mistake political opinions for definitive religious rulings.
"Sometimes in politics, the fatwa changes every two years. But people think it comes from a religious teacher, so they follow it. In fact, it is a political opinion," he said.
Anwar said social media made it easy for people to pass themselves off as experts and offer religious interpretations for political ends, whether they were in government or in opposition.
He said questioning sources was part of Islamic scholarly tradition.
"If you cite a hadith, people ask which one. Which verse of the Quran? Whose commentary are you using?" he added.

Title: Fadhlina: Students must master basics alongside AI literacy
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Education Ministry is committed to teaching teachers and students to use artificial intelligence (AI) ethically and responsibly, while ensuring they continue to master basic skills such as reading, writing and arithmetic.
Its minister, Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek, said the introduction of this technology in schools is not intended to encourage students to rely on AI to complete all school assignments, but rather to educate them about its limitations and ethical use.
"I understand the concerns of parents and teachers that dependence on this technology can make children lazy to read and lose their creativity. That concern is valid.
"However, educating children about AI also means educating them about the ethics of its use," she said in a Facebook post.
Fadhlina said she had accompanied Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim to the launch of the National Education Artificial Intelligence (AI) Initiative, dubbed AI Temu AI, today.
She said the launch of the Digital Educational Learning Initiative Malaysia (Delima) 3.0 and the AI Literacy Guide was aimed at ensuring educators and students could understand and apply the technology safely.
She also welcomed the introduction of Cikgu ILMU by YTL AI Labs in collaboration with Universiti Malaya, describing cooperation between the government and industry as crucial to ensuring that the technology developed met the needs of the national education ecosystem.
Fadhlina said the reading culture and development of students' character must continue to be strengthened alongside technological advancements.
"I also believe that no matter how advanced technology becomes, it will never be able to replace the human touch of a teacher in educating children.
"In facing the era of AI, the responsibility of the MoE is to ensure that our children do not fall behind in mastering technology without sacrificing the fundamental aspects of their education," she added.

Title: Basic treatment fees at public health facilities to stay unchanged
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Basic treatment fees at public hospitals and clinics should stay at current rates to avoid burdening low-income patients, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said tonight.
He said there was no basis for raising the fees because wages had yet to keep pace with economic growth and the cost of living.
"What's the basis for charging RM10? If people can afford it, I agree. High earners who opt for a first-class ward in a government hospital could pay more.
"Even though inflation is low, should we raise taxes or fees for ordinary people? I'm not prepared to do that," he said on RTM's Dialog Negara programme aired on TV1 and RTMKlik tonight, which was also simulcast on Bernama TV, Astro AWANI, TV3, TV AlHijrah and TVS.
Subsidised outpatient fees at Health Ministry facilities are currently RM1 for general treatment and RM5 for specialist services.
Anwar, who is also Finance Minister, said healthcare remained the second-largest recipient of funding under the Madani Budget, behind education, which reflected the government's commitment to improving the welfare of healthcare workers and the quality of public health services.
He said the government would stop hiring doctors on contract from Jan 1 next year, and that the savings of tens of billions of ringgit from tighter oversight and efforts to tackle corruption and the loss of public funds had helped make the decision possible.
"When we decided to end contract hiring for doctors, it meant we had new funding available. These sham contracts have to stop. Some people don't like it when I call it sakau (looting), but that's what it is.
"They don't realise we've saved tens of billions of ringgit by tightening oversight. There was no discussion, and they took RM200 million to RM300 million under the table. There must be a tender. We're returning this money to the people," he said.
Anwar said the savings had allowed the government to fund major programmes without raising taxes or cutting basic subsidies. He cited RM16 billion for Sumbangan Tunai Rahmah (STR) and Sumbangan Asas Rahmah (SARA), RM18 billion for civil service pay adjustments and RM40 billion to maintain fuel subsidies.
Anwar also stressed the need to deploy doctors to rural and remote areas, and urged Malaysians to cut back on sugar and exercise regularly to help curb rising rates of non-communicable diseases such as diabetes and obesity.
The panellists at the dialogue included Komuniti Pejuang Hartanah founder Datuk Ahyat Ishak, KRA group strategy director Amir Fareed Rahim, medical officer and social media influencer Dr Malar Santhi Santherasegapan, and entrepreneur and digital content creator Adam Shamil.

Title: Govt mulls stricter checks on imported online goods
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The government is looking at measures to ensure imported products sold through e-commerce platforms meet minimum quality and safety standards, in a move to protect consumers and ensure fair competition for local manufacturers.
Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani said the matter was discussed with Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Minister Datuk Armizan Mohd Ali to address the growing availability of imported products sold online without proper quality certification.
He said while the government encouraged consumers to embrace e-commerce, it was equally important to ensure products entering the Malaysian market complied with the necessary standards.
"Products are coming in from overseas through e-commerce, arriving in parcels. Some of these products are cheap but do not have quality certification or even Sirim certification.
"Some electrical goods also do not have certification. This is something we need to look into," he said after delivering his keynote address at the 2026 Majlis Sirim Industri.
Johari said consumers risked spending money on products that appeared to offer value for money but deteriorated or stopped functioning after only a few months.
He said the government needed to work with other ministries and agencies, including the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC), to determine how online platforms could be held accountable for ensuring products sold through their services met the required standards.
"I have discussed this with Armizan. We want to find a way for Miti and the Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Ministry to work together to address this issue.
"While we encourage people to buy goods online, there must be some standard requirements that these products have to meet.
"If platforms do not take these standards into consideration, we may ask MCMC to consider what action needs to be taken," he said.
Johari said imported products should be subject to appropriate requirements, just as locally manufactured goods had to undergo testing and certification to demonstrate compliance.
He said this would ensure local manufacturers, who incurred costs to have their products tested and certified, were not disadvantaged by cheaper imported alternatives that bypassed similar requirements.
In his keynote address, Johari said Malaysia remained committed to addressing the importation and sale of non-compliant products, which exposed consumers to potential health and safety risks while undermining the competitiveness of domestic industries.
"Malaysian manufacturers invest considerable resources in testing, certification and quality assurance to comply with our regulatory requirements.
"We cannot allow these investments to be undermined by imported products that gain an unfair cost advantage by circumventing the very same requirements," he said.
He said standards, testing, inspection and certification played an important role in helping Malaysian companies improve their capabilities, gain access to international markets and participate in global supply chains.
Johari also called for Sirim's testing and certification services to remain accessible, cost-effective and responsive to industry needs while maintaining technical rigour and integrity.
Meanwhile, he congratulated Sirim QAS International on becoming the first National Certification Body in Malaysia and Southeast Asia to receive accreditation for AS9110 Quality Management System (QMS) requirements for Aviation Maintenance Organisations.
He said the achievement was a significant milestone for Malaysia's aerospace ecosystem as it strengthened domestic conformity assessment capabilities and facilitated access to internationally recognised certification services for maintenance, repair and overhaul companies.

Title: 16 organ transplants performed in five days following four donations
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Sixteen organ and tissue transplants were successfully performed nationwide over five days following donations from four brain-dead donors.
Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad said the donations involved Universiti Sains Malaysia Hospital, Melaka Hospital, Shah Alam Hospital and Sultanah Aminah Hospital in Johor Baru.
He said the generosity of the donors and their families had given patients a second chance at life, enabling eight kidney transplants, three liver transplants, one heart transplant and four corneal transplants.
Selayang Hospital and Kuala Lumpur Hospital each carried out four kidney transplants.
"My highest respects and deepest condolences go to the donors and their families. Your courage in making the most noble decision at a time of grief has given others in need a second chance at life," he said in a post on X.
He also urged those who had pledged to donate their organs to inform their families of their wishes.
Dzulkefly also thanked healthcare personnel at the National Transplant Centre (NTC) and the transplant teams at the hospitals involved, including surgeons, anaesthesiology teams, transplant coordinators, nurses, pharmacists and support staff.
He said the Health Ministry remained committed to strengthening and expanding organ transplant services nationwide through the establishment of the National Transplant Council, which held its inaugural meeting on Nov 2.

Title: Jom Bantu CSR initiative focuses on environmental conservation
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Thirty native trees were planted and 700 lampam fish fingerlings released into Tasik Metropolitan Kepong under the latest Jom Bantu corporate social responsibility (CSR) initiative.
Karnival Jom Heboh project director Eileen Lim said the initiative, supported by Affin Bank, expanded the scope of the carnival's CSR programme to include environmental conservation.
She said previous Jom Bantu initiatives had focused on helping vulnerable groups, including senior citizens and orphans, while this year's programme placed emphasis on restoring the environment.
"Jom Bantu is a corporate social responsibility initiative carried out every time Karnival Jom Heboh takes place in different states.
"Previously, we had contributed to senior citizens and orphans. This time, it is the environment's turn.
"We are proud of and grateful to Affin Bank for always supporting the Jom Bantu initiative," she said after the Jom Bantu CSR programme with Affin Bank, held in conjunction with the 2026 Karnival Jom Heboh Kuala Lumpur at Taman Tasik Metropolitan Kepong.
The programme, held in collaboration with Kuala Lumpur City Hall (DBKL) from 3pm to 5pm, also included fertilising existing trees in the park.
Also present were Affin Bank Group Corporate Events and Collaboration, Strategic Communications manager Fatin Atiqa Hassan; Affin Bank Financing Sales head Qamarul Jamly Abdul Jamal; Taman Tasik Metropolitan Kepong landscape architect Anuar Ahmad; and, park representative Sharifah Dora Syed Mohamad.
Eileen said the initiative was also aimed at raising public awareness of environmental conservation and encouraging more corporate bodies and members of the public to contribute to the community.
"With this Jom Bantu initiative, as we travel to each state, we hope more corporations and members of the public will join us in finding ways to give back.
"We can help the people, the ecosystem and the environment," she said.
