Title: Examinations Board: No leak in SPM Pendidikan Moral paper
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The alleged leak of the Sijil Pelajaran Malaysia (SPM) Pendidikan Moral examination paper does not meet the definition of an examination leak under the National Assessment Policy, the Examinations Board said.
It said this was based on the National Assessment Policy, Third Edition 2023.
The board said its checks found that the social media post was uploaded at 11.44am, after the examination ended at 10.45am.
It said the examination paper was a classified document with confidential status.
"Taking photographs, copying or disseminating the contents of an examination paper without permission constitutes a breach of procedures governing the handling of classified documents.
"Such actions may also be subject to action under the Official Secrets Act 1972, subject to the outcome of investigations by the authorities," it said in a statement.
A social media post claiming that the examination paper was leaked went viral earlier today.
The board said further investigations were under way and that monitoring at examination centres had been stepped up in cooperation with state education departments and district education offices.
It said it took the allegation seriously.
"Any party affected by the post is also encouraged to lodge a police report to enable the authorities to investigate and take appropriate action in accordance with the law," it said.
The board urged the public not to spread information or speculate on the matter, as this could cause confusion and anxiety among candidates, parents and the wider community.
It said it remained committed to safeguarding the integrity, confidentiality and credibility of public examinations, as well as protecting the interests and rights of all candidates.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Anwar remembers A. Samad Said's courage, love for language and literature
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim remembers National Laureate Datuk Seri A. Samad Said for his steadfast principles and deep love for language and literature.
In a post on X today, Anwar said the writer had taught that the strength of language and literature could help build a brave and dignified nation.
"That spirit will continue to accompany our steps in this struggle. Rest in peace, Pak Samad. Al-Fatihah," he said.
Anwar also recalled hearing the late writer recite his poem Di Atas Padang Sejarah at Stadium Merdeka here during the Himpunan Kebangkitan Rakyat rally about 13 years ago.
"Before tens of thousands of people gathered there, the verses of his poem ignited our spirit to keep rising and dare to speak out against tyranny.
"When the people's voices were being silenced and the machinery of government was used to suppress those who dared to speak up, Pak Samad chose to fight back with poetry," he said.
A. Samad died at 6.10pm yesterday after receiving treatment at Hospital Kuala Lumpur due to age-related ailments and diabetes.
Born on April 9, 1935, in Kampung Belimbing Dalam, Durian Tunggal, Melaka, he was the fourth recipient of the National Literary Award in 1985.
He was renowned for literary works including the novels Salina, Sungai Mengalir Lesu and Hujan Pagi.
Anwar had paid his last respects to the laureate at Masjid Saidina Abu Bakar As-Siddiq in Bangsar.
A. Samad was laid to rest at the Bukit Kiara Muslim Cemetery at 10.55am.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: BFood narrows quarterly loss to RM4.66mil
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Berjaya Food Bhd's (BFood) net loss narrowed to RM4.66 million in the first quarter ended Sept 30, 2026 (Q1 FY27), from RM14.80 million a year earlier.
This followed BFood's store rationalisation and cost management initiatives.
Despite operating fewer stores in Malaysia during the quarter, the group said it recorded marginally higher revenue.
Revenue for the quarter edged up to RM128.54 million from RM128.25 million previously, while loss per share narrowed to 0.24 sen from 0.84 sen.
This was supported by positive same-store sales growth at Starbucks Malaysia and stronger sales from its overseas operations.
BFood said the improved performance, particularly at Starbucks Malaysia, marked an encouraging milestone in its recovery, reflecting progress from business rationalisation, cost optimisation and strategic marketing initiatives.
The group will focus on building on the momentum by improving store productivity, driving revenue growth and continuing cost optimisation across its operations.
Despite prevailing business challenges, management remains focused on strengthening the group's financial position and sustaining its recovery to deliver long-term growth and better returns to shareholders.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: No more visa-free entry for Indians from Jan 1 as Malaysia tightens pre-arrival checks
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 25 — The Immigration Department of Malaysia has announced that the visa exemption for Indian nationals ends on Jan 1, 2027.
From that date, Indian nationals must obtain a valid visa before entering Malaysia. Applications can be submitted through the MyVISA portal from Dec 1, 2026.
In a statement posted on Facebook today, the department said all visa processing fees paid are non-refundable, regardless of the outcome of the application, any change in policy, or any subsequent change to travel plans.
“The Immigration Department reserves the right to amend these entry conditions at any time in accordance with the directives of the Government of Malaysia.
“Indian nationals entering Malaysia from that date must obtain a valid visa before arrival,” the statement read.
Last Friday, the media reported Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail as saying the visa exemption for Indian nationals on 30-day stays for short-term social visits will end on Dec 31.
He said the termination of the initiative under the Visa Liberalisation Plan aimed to strengthen pre-arrival screening and ensure more orderly entry control over foreigners. — Bernama

Title: Ramanan says Nepal tragedy families may get long-awaited closure with death certificates due in December
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 25 — Certificates of presumed death for the victims of the flood and landslide tragedy in Nepal are expected to be issued as early as December, once the authorities in that country provide the relevant documentation to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.
Human Resources Minister Datuk Seri R. Ramanan said the National Registration Department (NRD) will carry out the issuance process as soon as it receives the verification documents from the Government of Nepal.
“I have received confirmation from the director-general of NRD (Datuk Badrul Hisham Alias) that once the documentation received from the Nepalese side is forwarded by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, he is prepared to issue the certificates as quickly as possible.
“We anticipate that the process can be completed as early as December,” he said during a press conference following a ceremony to present aid to the families of the victims of the flood and landslide tragedy in Nepal, held at Menara Pertubuhan Keselamatan Sosial here today.
Also present were SOCSO chief executive officer Datuk Seri Dr. Mohammed Azman Aziz Mohammed, co-founder of Solidariti Malaysia: Keluarga Dalam Harapan (Masfih) Dr. Manivannan Rethinam, and family members of the tragedy’s victims.
In the Dewan Rakyat (Parliament) today, Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail explained that the declaration of presumed death for the 54 Malaysians missing in the Nepal flood tragedy is entirely subject to the legal procedures and administrative mechanisms of that country.
He noted that the NRD can only issue an official death certificate under the Births and Deaths Registration Act 1957 (Act 299) once the authorities at the incident site have provided prior verification. — Bernama

Title: Infant hospitalised after being picked up from babysitter’s home, police launch probe
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 25 — Police are investigating a neglect case involving a five-month-old baby girl who was found unconscious and suffering from seizures after being picked up by her mother from a babysitter’s home recently.
Kuala Lumpur Police Chief Datuk Fadil Marsus said that in addition to seizures, preliminary examinations on the infant also revealed bruises and wounds on her face and ears.
He said police received a report regarding the incident from a medical officer at Hospital Canselor Tuanku Muhriz (HCTM) after the victim’s mother brought the baby to the hospital’s Emergency Department for treatment on Nov 14.
“The victim is currently placed at the Tunku Ampuan Besar Tuanku Aishah Rohani Hospital, Universiti Kebangsaan Malaysia Children’s Specialist Hospital (HPKK UKM), for monitoring and further examination,” he said in a statement today.
Fadil said the case is being investigated under Section 31(1)(a) of the Child Act 2001 and further investigations are still underway.
“In this regard, the public is advised not to make any speculation or spread unverified posts on social media as such actions could jeopardise the investigation process,” he said.
Anyone with information regarding the incident is urged to contact the Kuala Lumpur Police Hotline at 03-2115 9999 or go to the nearest police station to assist in the investigation. — Bernama

Title: After RM4.8m meth bust, Mindef moves to protect RMAF personnel who made arrests
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 25 — The Ministry of Defence (Mindef) is protecting Royal Malaysian Air Force (RMAF) personnel who arrested suspects in a drug trafficking syndicate that used military transport facilities in the Klang Valley and Labuan recently.
Deputy Defence Minister Adly Zahari said the ministry will shield all RMAF personnel cooperating with the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) in further investigations.
“We will certainly cooperate with the investigation. At the same time, we recognise our responsibility at the RMAF level. The safety of our officers who made these arrests is something we are addressing, because this is no small matter,” he said in the Dewan Rakyat today.
He said this when winding up the committee-stage debate on the Supply Bill (Budget) 2027 and the Development Expenditure Estimates Motion 2027 for the Ministry of Defence.
Last week, police busted a drug trafficking syndicate using military transport facilities in operations across the Klang Valley and Labuan, seizing 96.64 kg of methamphetamine valued at RM4.83 million and 6.98 kg of liquid chemical.
On the latest developments, Adly said 13 individuals had been detained so far, seven of them RMAF personnel, comprising three captains, two lieutenants, a warrant officer II and an air corporal.
He said that apart from an internal probe, the Ministry would give PDRM room to conduct a detailed investigation without any information leak, so that the syndicate’s network could be fully dismantled.
On a separate matter, Adly said the proposal to extend the National Service Training Programme (PLKN) from 45 days to 90 or 180 days requires further study, including the government’s financial capacity.
“For PLKN going forward, the government has so far identified 13 military camp sites, some of which have been and are being upgraded in phases, involving an allocation of RM80 million,” he said.
The Dewan Rakyat then approved RM22.108 billion in operating and development expenditure for MINDEF under Budget 2027, after 23 MPs debated it and a majority voted in favour. — Bernama

Title: ‘When others were silenced, Pak Samad fought back with poetry,’ says Anwar
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 25 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said he will always remember the late National Laureate Datuk Seri A. Samad Said’s steadfastness in upholding his principles and his deep love for language and literature.
In a post on X today, Anwar said the late laureate taught that the strength of language and literature can build a brave and dignified nation.
“That spirit will continue to accompany our steps in this struggle. Rest in peace, Pak Samad. Al-Fatihah,” he said.
The Prime Minister also recalled hearing the late writer’s voice reciting the poem Di Atas Padang Sejarah at Stadium Merdeka here during the Himpunan Kebangkitan Rakyat rally, about 13 years ago.
“Before tens of thousands of people gathered there, the verses of his poem ignited our spirit to keep rising and dare to speak out against tyranny.
“When the people’s voices were being silenced and the machinery of government was used to suppress those who dared to speak up, Pak Samad chose to fight back with poetry,” he said.
A. Samad breathed his last at 6.10pm yesterday after receiving treatment at Hospital Kuala Lumpur (HKL) due to old age, in addition to suffering from diabetes.
Born on April 9, 1935, in Kampung Belimbing Dalam, Durian Tunggal, Melaka, he was the fourth recipient of the National Literary Award in 1985 and was renowned for masterpieces such as the novels Salina, Sungai Mengalir Lesu, and Hujan Pagi.
Yesterday, the Prime Minister attended to pay his last respects to the late laureate at Masjid Saidina Abu Bakar As-Siddiq in Bangsar.
A. Samad was laid to rest at the Bukit Kiara Muslim Cemetery here at 10.55am today. — Bernama

Title: ‘No plans as of today’: Wan Rosdy dismisses talk of early Pahang election
Article:
KUANTAN, Nov 25 — Pahang Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Wan Rosdy Wan Ismail today said he had no plans to dissolve the State Legislative Assembly (DUN) to pave the way for a state election.
“There are no plans as of today,” he said briefly at the Pahang State Legislative Assembly sitting at Wisma Sri Pahang here.
He was responding to a question from Datuk Seri Tuan Ibrahim Tuan Man (PN-Cheka), who wanted to know whether the Pahang DUN would be dissolved following remarks by several assemblymen suggesting that the current sitting could be their last.
Tuan Ibrahim raised the question while interjecting during the debate on the Pahang 2027 Budget by Datuk Seri Shafik Fauzan Sharif (BN-Inderapura), who had described the sitting as his ‘final days’ as the Inderapura assemblyman after 22 years in the post since 2004.
Shafik Fauzan also said he had no intention of defending the Inderapura state seat in the next general election (GE16).
Meanwhile, when met by reporters, Tuan Ibrahim said there had been no formal discussions so far on cooperation with Pahang Barisan Nasional (BN).
“Not yet. We are sounding them out first. PAS leaders in each state have been instructed to hold meetings at all levels to explore ways to advance the agenda of unity of the ummah,” he said.
BN was previously reported to be in no hurry to call elections in other states despite recording positive momentum in several state elections, including in Melaka recently.
However, BN chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said any decision on calling an election would be left to the respective state leaders to assess whether the time was right. — Bernama

Title: Private university student claims trial over Jalan Jelatek crash that killed retired military personnel
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 25 — A private university student pleaded not guilty in the Magistrate’s Court today to a charge of reckless driving that resulted in the death of a retired military personnel on Jalan Jelatek here last Saturday.
The accused, a 32-year-old Libyan national, Ali Abdul Rahman Mahmoud Elmaki, entered his plea after the charge was read to him in English before Magistrate Amalina Johar.
According to the charge, the man allegedly drove a Proton Saga recklessly and dangerously, causing the death of 43-year-old Mohd Hairezam Omar on Jalan Jelatek from the direction of Wangsa Maju towards Taman Keramat at 1 am on Nov 21.
The charge is brought under Section 41(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987, which carries a maximum fine of RM50,000 or imprisonment for up to 10 years. Additionally, a conviction under this section would result in an endorsement on the offender’s driving license.
Deputy Public Prosecutor Mohamad Fadhly Mohd Zamry objected to the granting of bail, citing the fact that the accused is a foreign national and that the offence committed is of a serious nature.
“However, should the court choose to exercise its discretion to grant bail under Section 388 of the Criminal Procedure Code, the prosecution proposes bail at RM70,000 with two Malaysian sureties.
“The prosecution also requests additional conditions: that the accused’s passport be surrendered to the court, that he reports to the nearest police station at least once a month, and that he is prohibited from using his driving license until the conclusion of the case. I request that the court consider these conditions should bail be granted, given that the accused is a foreign national and poses a flight risk,” said Mohamad Fadhly.
Defence counsel K. Ramalingam, representing the accused, requested a lower bail amount around RM10,000 on the grounds that his client is a Master’s degree student who is scheduled to sit for examinations next month.
“The accused resides in Malaysia with his wife and has a permanent address on Jalan Ampang. He is also prepared to accept all additional conditions requested by the prosecution,” he said.
The court subsequently granted bail at RM17,000 with two Malaysian sureties, subject to additional conditions that the accused must surrender his passport to the court, report to a nearby police station once a month, and have his driver’s license suspended until the conclusion of the case.
The court has set January 28 of next year for the next mention of the case.
Previously, media reports indicated that the victim, who was riding a motorcycle from the direction of Taman Keramat toward Setiawangsa, was struck by a car driven by a Libyan national coming from the direction of Wangsa Maju, who had failed to stop at a red traffic light.
The victim, who sustained severe injuries, was pronounced dead at the scene, while alcohol and urine screening tests conducted on the driver returned negative results. — Bernama

Title: Tides rising, storms brewing: Penang residents advised to monitor weather closely
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Nov 25 — Residents in low-lying areas and near the coast have been advised to increase their level of preparedness following the forecast of high tides, rain and thunderstorms in most areas of the state until Friday (Nov 27).
Penang Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) director Mohamad Shoki Hamzah said the public should take note of the high and low tide schedule for George Town and Penang Port, particularly those living in flood-prone areas.
“High tide is forecast at 12.52am tomorrow, reaching 2.68 metres (m), while the water level is expected to reach 2.23m at 1.25pm.
“Based on the forecast, the highest tide level on Friday is expected to reach 2.71m at 1.29am, while the level is forecast to reach 2.19m at 2.07 pm,” he told Bernama when contacted today.
Meanwhile, he urged the public to also pay attention to weather conditions, as the Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has forecast thunderstorms in most areas in the afternoon and rain in most places at night from today until Friday.
Mohamad Shoki said rain is expected in several areas tomorrow morning, before thunderstorms hit most parts of the state in the afternoon, followed by rain at night.
He said similar weather conditions are forecast for Friday, with no rain expected in the morning, before thunderstorms hit most places in the afternoon and rain at night.
“Although no continuous rain warning has been issued for Penang so far, residents should remain alert to weather developments and instructions from the authorities throughout the Northeast Monsoon (MTL) season,” he added.
He said members of the public facing emergencies should contact the 24-hour 999 emergency hotline, and obtain weather and safety information through the Penang JBPM official social media channels. — Bernama

Title: Pantai Remis teen charged with murdering newborn daughter, boyfriend admits helping bury infant
Article:
TAIPING, Nov 25 — A female teenager was brought before the Magistrate’s Court here today on a charge of murdering her newborn baby girl by stabbing the infant last week.
Nurul Iman Najiha Abdullah, 19, nodded in understanding when the charge against her was read out before Magistrate R. Prabakaran.
However, no plea was recorded from the accused on the murder charge as the case falls under the jurisdiction of the High Court.
Nurul Iman Najiha was charged with murdering a baby girl, who was her biological child, in an oil palm area behind a house in Kampung Panchor, Pantai Remis, in the Larut, Matang and Selama district, between Nov 14 and 16.
The charge was framed under Section 302 of the Penal Code, which carries the death penalty or imprisonment of not less than 30 years and not exceeding 40 years, and if not sentenced to death, shall also be punished with whipping of not less than 12 strokes, upon conviction.
Meanwhile, in a separate charge, Nurul Iman Najiha and her boyfriend, Mohamad Aidil Eikmal, 19, were jointly charged with common intention to conceal the birth of the baby girl by secretly burying the infant’s body at the same location and dates.
They were charged under Section 318 of the Penal Code, read together with Section 34 of the same code, which provides for a maximum prison sentence of two years, or a fine, or both, upon conviction.
Mohamad Aidil pleaded guilty to the charge, while Nurul Iman Najiha pleaded not guilty.
Deputy Public Prosecutor Farihah Adilah Faizal requested bail at RM50,000 with one surety for each accused, while no bail was offered for the murder charge faced by Nurul Iman Najiha.
Meanwhile, counsel from the National Legal Aid Foundation (YBGK) Nurul Hanis Mohd Zaini, representing both accused, appealed for lower bail as this was their first offence and the couple worked as an eatery assistant and a construction labourer respectively.
“Nurul Iman Najiha also has mental health issues but has never sought treatment,” the lawyer said.
The court then set bail at RM5,000 with two sureties for each accused and fixed Jan 4 for re-mention of the case for Nurul Iman Najiha to appoint a lawyer, as well as for a social report from the Social Welfare Department for Mohamad Aidil before sentencing him.
On Nov 19, Perak Police Chief Datuk Mohd Alwi Zainal Abidin said a newborn baby girl died after allegedly being stabbed by her biological mother in an incident in Pantai Remis on Nov 14.
He said preliminary investigations found that the 19-year-old teenager committed the act at her home before contacting her boyfriend to help bury the baby’s body behind the house. — Bernama

Title: Fuel prices take a dive: RON97, unsubsidised RON95 and diesel all down 25 sen
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 25 — Retail prices of RON97, unsubsidised RON95 and unsubsidised diesel will all fall by 25 sen per litre from Nov 26 to Dec 2.
The Finance Ministry (MOF) said today that under the Automatic Pricing Mechanism (APM) formula, RON97 will drop from RM4.00 to RM3.75 per litre, while unsubsidised RON95 will fall from RM3.72 to RM3.47 per litre.
The retail price of unsubsidised diesel will fall from RM4.72 to RM4.47 per litre.
According to MOF, refined petroleum product prices in regional markets moderated during the APM calculation period, easing price pressure in the international petroleum market.
“At the same time, prospects of higher global crude oil supply also contributed to lower world oil prices. However, refined petroleum supplies still face constraints in certain markets.
“Geopolitical uncertainty and risks of petroleum delivery disruptions could still affect global supply. Therefore, world oil prices are expected to continue fluctuating in the near term,” the statement said.
Meanwhile, it said the Madani government remains committed to protecting the people and businesses through targeted fuel subsidies under Budi Madani, with nearly RM40 billion allocated for fuel subsidies next year to ease cost-of-living pressures.
Under Budi95, eligible recipients will continue paying RM1.99 per litre for RON95 compared with the unsubsidised price of RM3.47 per litre, with the government subsidising RM1.48 per litre, or 43 per cent of the unsubsidised price.
For Budi Diesel, eligible recipients will continue paying RM2.10 per litre against the unsubsidised price of RM4.47 per litre, with the government subsidising RM2.37 per litre, or 53 per cent of the unsubsidised price.
Subsidised fuel prices under the Subsidised Petrol Control System (SKPS) remain unchanged at RM2.05 per litre, while the Subsidised Diesel Control System (SKDS) stays at RM2.15 per litre.
MOF said eligible Malaysians can continue buying subsidised RON95 and diesel using their MyKad under Budi95 and Budi Diesel, subject to monthly eligibility limits. — Bernama

Title: Terengganu emerges from floods, Selangor braces as evacuee count approaches 1,000
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 25 — Terengganu closed its last flood relief centre this afternoon, while the number of evacuees in Selangor rose to 958 and the figure in Perak remained at 211.
In TERENGGANU, all 151 evacuees at Dewan Serbaguna Tok Jembal in Kuala Nerus were allowed to return home after floodwaters receded, and the centre closed at 2pm, the state flood disaster management secretariat said.
The secretariat said it remained on alert as a heavy rain warning for the state was in effect until Friday.
The Social Welfare Department’s InfoBencana portal reported that the water level at the Kampung Bukit (F1) station in Setiu remained at the alert level after exceeding 10.5 metres.
In SELANGOR, 958 people from 281 families were sheltering at relief centres this afternoon, up from 819 people from 228 families this morning.
According to InfoBencana, nine relief centres were operating in Selangor, with four in Kuala Selangor, two in Kuala Langat and three in Sepang, the latest district to be hit by floods.
All three centres in Sepang opened today, with Dewan Orang Ramai Kampung Dato Ahmad Razali sheltering 122 people, Dewan Orang Ramai Dengkil 49 and Dewan Orang Ramai Taman Gemilang 15.
In Kuala Selangor, Sekolah Kebangsaan (SK) Dato’ Maharaja Lela housed 313 evacuees, Sekolah Rendah Agama Pasangan 158, Sekolah Agama Batu 8 Ijok 108 and Dewan Orang Ramai Bukit Kuching Tengah 30.
The two centres in Kuala Langat were SK RTB Bukit Changgang, with 147 evacuees, and Balai Raya Kampung Sungai Kelambu, with 16.
In PERAK, 211 people from 63 families remained at three relief centres in three districts this afternoon, unchanged from this morning.
The Perak State Disaster Management Committee secretariat said Sekolah Rendah Agama Rakyat Padang Serai in Manjung housed 127 evacuees from 37 families.
Dewan Rumah Rehat Majlis Perbandaran Teluk Intan in Hilir Perak housed 74 people from 22 families, while 10 people from four families remained at SK Batu Hampar in Larut, Matang and Selama district.
The Department of Irrigation and Drainage said Sungai Kurau at the Bukit Merah reservoir in Kerian was at the danger level, with a reading of 9.17 metres against the normal level of 8.68 metres.
The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) forecast rain tonight in all Perak districts except Manjung. — Bernama

Title: Fisherman pleads not guilty to insulting ‘hadis’, spreading teachings contrary to Islamic law
Article:
MANJUNG, Nov 25 — A fisherman pleaded not guilty in the Syariah High Court here today to two charges of insulting the hadis and expounding religious teachings contrary to Islamic law about two years ago.
Mazlan Abd Shukor, 69, who is said to be a leader and teacher of the Millah Abraham deviant sect in Manjung district, entered the plea after both charges were read out before Judge Mohd Ridzuan Yusof.
According to the first charge, he allegedly insulted the hadis by uttering the words, “Kalau kita pakai hadis itu kata orang. Kata orang tak semestinya betul” (If we rely on the hadis, that is what people say. What people say is not necessarily true), at a house in Pantai Remis between 11 am and noon on April 26, 2024.
The charge was framed under Section 15 of the Syariah Criminal Enactment 1992, which provides for a maximum fine of RM5,000 or imprisonment for up to three years, or both, upon conviction.
On the second count, Mazlan allegedly expounded religious teachings contrary to Islamic law to his two daughters, Maisarah, 23, and Maryam Sakinah, 20, by saying, “Quran dia memang kena baca dalam bahasa kita bukannya dibaca dalam bahasa itu” (The Quran should be read in our own language, not in that language), at the same place, time and date.
The charge, under Section 9 of the same enactment, carries a maximum fine of RM5,000 or imprisonment for up to three years, or both, upon conviction.
Syariah prosecutor Amir Sabri Zulkipli proposed bail of RM5,000 in one surety for each charge, arguing that offences involving matters of Islamic faith were serious.
The accused appealed for a lower bail amount on the grounds that he was still supporting two children pursuing higher education.
Mohd Ridzuan then set bail at RM3,000 in one surety and fixed Jan 13 next year for mention. — Bernama

Title: Flood-hit Shah Alam gets immediate relief as Putrajaya rolls out three projects, eyes bigger RM40m fix
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 25 — The government, through the Selangor Department of Irrigation and Drainage (DID), is implementing three immediate mitigation measures to reduce flood risks in Shah Alam, with construction work expected to be completed between February and March next year.
Deputy Minister of Energy Transition and Water Transformation Datuk Seri Abdul Rahman Mohamad said the first project involves the construction of a flood wall and the installation of a flap gate at Taman Rashna, at a cost of RM350,000, with completion scheduled for March 17, 2027.
The second project entails the construction of an outlet structure, the installation of a flap gate, and the building of a flood wall near the Bukit Raja junction, at a cost of RM199,000, with completion scheduled for Feb 17, 2027.
“Third, there is the construction of a flood wall at Taman Intan, costing RM200,000, which is also scheduled for completion on Feb 17, 2027,” he said during a Special Chamber session in the Dewan Rakyat today.
He was responding to a question from Azli Yusof (PH-Shah Alam) regarding the status of flood control plans for the Sungai Rasah Basin, following recent flash flood incidents.
Abdul Rahman added that DID has also deployed six mobile pump units across four high-risk locations namely Taman Rashna, Taman Intan, the area near the Bukit Raja junction, and the AEON supermarket to accelerate the drainage of floodwaters, thereby reducing the duration of water stagnation.
For the long term, he said the government has approved an allocation of RM40 million under the First Rolling Plan of the 13th Malaysia Plan (13MP) for the construction of a water control gate at the estuary of the Sungai Rasah, as well as a pump house, a flood retention basin, and riverbank retaining walls.
“The project is currently in the preliminary design stage, with physical works targeted to commence in the second quarter of 2028 and expected to be completed by 2031,” he said.
Abdul Rahman noted that the ministry has also proposed splitting the RM40 million allocation into two separate tenders to accelerate the project’s implementation, potentially shortening the construction period to 2029, ahead of the original 2031 target.
He explained that a key focus will be preventing water from the Sungai Klang from overflowing into high-risk areas in Shah Alam and this component is estimated to cost between RM15 million and RM20 million, depending on the final scope and the findings of technical studies.
“Overall, the planning for these components aims to enhance the capacity of the flood control system in the Sungai Rasah Basin, making it more integrated and effective.
“These measures are expected to reduce the risk and impact of flooding on residents and the surrounding areas; however, the final scope of the project remains subject to the results of studies and detailed designs prepared by the consultants,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Three girls found after string of teenage disappearances in Kota Kinabalu, search continues for 16-year-old Olivia Jeffrey
Article:
KOTA KINABALU, Nov 25 — Three of the four teenage girls reported missing in separate incidents in the district have been found, with only one still missing.
In a statement today, Kota Kinabalu district police headquarters (IPD) said the three girls who have been found are Lorna Palmani, 17, Nadyana Albaser, 16, and Farha Nabila Abdullah, 14.
Meanwhile, Olivia Jeffrey, 16, of Taman Richdar, Menggatal, who was reported missing since November 7, has yet to be found, and police are continuing their search for the teenager.
Members of the public with information on Olivia Jeffrey’s whereabouts are urged to contact the Kota Kinabalu IPD at 088-529222 or the nearest police station. — Bernama

Title: Banting son charged with mother’s murder, back in court Jan 19 next year
Article:
KUALA LANGAT, Nov 25 — An unemployed man, 27, has been charged with murdering his mother at a house in Taman Banting Baru, Selangor.
S. M. Madavan was charged at the Telok Datok Magistrate’s Court yesterday with murdering V. Kanagavalli, 51, between 2.30am and 3.30am on November 13, Harian Metro reported today.
The charge, under Section 302 of the Penal Code, carries the death penalty or 30 to 40 years’ jail upon conviction.
If he is not sentenced to death, he must also be given at least 12 strokes of the cane.
The court did not allow bail and fixed January 19, 2027 for mention.
Deputy public prosecutor Muhammad Amirul Syafiq Yazid prosecuted.
Kuala Langat district police chief Superintendent Mohd Akmalrizal Radzi previously said on November 14 that the suspect, who was then held to assist investigations into his mother’s death, had tested positive for methamphetamine.
He said police learnt of the woman’s death through the MERS 999 emergency line, and the suspect was remanded for seven days.

Title: Sarawak election: Chong Chong Chieng Jen heads to Kota Sentosa, GPS hopeful Nicholas Wung says Padungan now a ‘level playing field’
Article:
KUCHING, Nov 25 — Gabungan Parti Sarawak (GPS) Padungan candidate Nicholas Wung Duk Ying said the contest in the constituency would be fairer now that incumbent Chong Chieng Jen has decided to return to his former seat of Kota Sentosa.
Wung, who is Sarawak United People’s Party (SUPP) Youth chief and acting secretary, said the Sarawak DAP’s decision to instead place Chong’s special assistant Michael Kong Feng Nian in the constituency would make the contest a more “level playing field” in terms of candidate age and seniority.
“I do not wish to be too presumptuous, but to me, Padungan is still an opposition stronghold, with DAP at the moment. We will try our best,” he said after GPS chairman Tan Sri Abang Johari Openg named him as the coalition’s pick for the seat.
Wung said he hoped to secure greater access to state resources and funding for the constituency if elected.
“Having a GPS assemblyman in the Padungan area would allow us to allocate more resources and funding from GPS.
“That would definitely benefit the 24,000 voters across the entire constituency. I think this has been lacking over the past 20 years, so let’s address the basic needs first,” he told reporters.
Wung, 40, is a lawyer who has been practising since 2011, mainly specialises in litigation work.
He joined SUPP about four years ago as a councillor and is contesting in an election for the first time.
During the 2021 state election, Chong won 4,686 votes in Padungan for a 1,198-vote majority over GPS’ Datuk Wee Hong Seng (3,488 votes), Parti Bumi Kenyalang’s Raymond Thong Ee Yu (930 votes), and Aspirasi’s Soo Lina (193 votes). — The Borneo Post

Title: PKR sits out Sarawak polls, but Lawas chief may not: Zahid Matserudin mulls solo run in Bukit Sari
Article:
MIRI, Nov 25 — Lawas PKR branch chief Zahid Matserudin is considering contesting the Bukit Sari seat as an independent candidate following his party’s decision not to take part in the 13th Sarawak state election.
Zahid, 35 said he had yet to make a final decision as he was still weighing several factors.
“I have already purchased my nomination form and am likely to contest as an independent. I have a few more days until nomination day to think about this,” he told The Borneo Post when contacted.
He admitted feeling disappointed with the party’s decision to sit out the election but said he respected the decision made by its top leadership.
Zahid had earlier expressed his readiness to contest in Bukit Sari, where the incumbent is caretaker deputy premier Datuk Awang Tengah Ali Hasan.
Awang Tengah is an eight-term assemblyman who first won the seat in 1987, when it was known as Lawas.
He was elected seven times under the Barisan Nasional (BN) ticket before retaining the seat under Gabungan Parti Sarawak (GPS) in the 2021 state election.
In the 2021 state election, Awang Tengah secured 6,385 votes and a majority of 5,636, defeating Alias Mail of the now-defunct Parti Sarawak Bersatu, who polled 749 votes, and Parti Bumi Kenyalang’s Riyah Basra, who received 165 votes. — The Borneo Post

Title: ‘Zero opposition’ a no-go, Chong Chieng Jen says as DAP fields 12 candidates in Sarawak polls
Article:
KUCHING, Nov 25 — Sarawak DAP will contest the 13th Sarawak election despite its Pakatan Harapan ally PKR deciding to sit out the polls.
Sarawak DAP chairman Chong Chieng Jen said the party had the autonomy to decide what was best for Sarawak and remained committed to providing a stronger opposition to keep the ruling Gabungan Parti Sarawak (GPS) in check.
He said PKR’s withdrawal made it even more important for DAP to remain in the electoral contest to ensure effective checks and balances in the State Legislative Assembly (DUN).
“Elections must not be seen as a destabilising force in any democratic society, but rather to reinforce the notion of check and balance (sic),” he said in a video message posted on Facebook.
For this coming election, DAP has finalised a 12-seat line-up, comprising Kota Sentosa, Batu Lintang, Padungan, Pending, Batu Kitang, Batu Kawa, Opar, Tanjong Batu, Pujut, Bukit Assek, Pelawan, and Meradong.
Among its candidates are Chong, who is returning to Kota Sentosa after representing the constituency from 2006 to 2021, Bandar Kuching MP Dr Kelvin Yii Lee Yuen in Batu Lintang, and incumbent Pending assemblywoman Violet Yong Wui Wui.
“We should not allow GPS to have absolute control of Sarawak’s DUN with zero opposition,” he said.
Chong alleged that Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim had given in to pressure from GPS to have PKR withdraw from the state election in exchange for the coalition’s continued support for the federal government.
He said GPS should use its political influence to expedite matters that would directly benefit ordinary Sarawakians.
With PKR’s withdrawal, Chong described DAP as the only opposition party in Sarawak with a long-standing record of remaining outside the ruling coalition.
He acknowledged the presence of other local opposition parties but questioned their ability to remain in opposition, citing past instances of elected representatives joining the ruling coalition after winning their seats.
He referred to former elected representatives from the Sarawak National Party and Parti Bansa Dayak Sarawak, who joined the then Sarawak Barisan Nasional, as well as former Parti Sarawak Bersatu representatives who had subsequently joined GPS.
In the previous 2021 state election, DAP contested 26 of the 82 seats but won only Padungan through Chong and Pending through Yong.
This was a significant decline from its performance in the 2016 election, when DAP won seven of the 31 seats contested.
Besides PKR, Barisan Nasional and Perikatan Nasional have also said they will not be contesting in the Sarawak polls. — The Borneo Post
*Editor’s note: DUN stands for Dewan Undangan Negeri (State Legislative Assembly).

Title: Malaysia wants more frequent Asean meetings to speed up disaster aid
Article:
TANGERANG, Nov 25 — Malaysia has proposed that senior Asean officials responsible for disaster management meet more often to improve coordination and speed up aid to member states hit by natural disasters.
Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said the proposal took into account the long interval before the next ministerial meeting, scheduled for October next year in Laos.
“We would like senior officials to meet more often, if possible, so that we can coordinate our efforts and get aid quickly to countries hit by natural disasters,” he told Bernama here today.
Ahmad Zahid was met after attending the 14th Asean Ministerial Meeting on Disaster Management (AMMDM), the 15th Meeting of the Conference of the Parties to the Asean Agreement on Disaster Management and Emergency Response (AADMER) and related meetings hosted by Indonesia.
Ahmad Zahid, who chairs the Central Disaster Management Committee, is on a five-day working visit to Indonesia and arrived in Jakarta on Tuesday after a series of meetings on rural development cooperation in Bali that began on Monday.
Ahmad Zahid said Asean member states had shown greater commitment to disaster management than in previous years, particularly in delivering aid on time and coordinating their responses.
“Aid has reached those affected on time, and we have seen Asean countries working together, whether or not they frequently experience disasters,” he said.
He said member states were also sharing their experience in managing disasters, particularly Indonesia, which hosts the Asean Coordinating Centre for Humanitarian Assistance on disaster management (AHA Centre) in Jakarta.
Timor-Leste, Asean’s newest member, had also shown its commitment by helping shape how member states coordinate and work together on disaster management, he said.
Ahmad Zahid said Laos, which will take over the AMMDM chairmanship next year, had begun putting previously agreed programmes into practice through a whole-of-government approach.
Ahmad Zahid said adopting new technology would help Asean prepare for the effects of climate change and global warming.
He said talks with Asean dialogue partners China, Japan and South Korea had offered fresh insights into early warning systems and the use of satellites to forecast rainfall and wind patterns.
“All Asean member states should adopt this new technology,” he said.
On haze, Ahmad Zahid said member states needed a common approach, although Malaysia had not raised the issue specifically at the meetings.
“We know we need to take new measures and use technology so that we can act before an incident occurs,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Nine districts, nine timetables: Selangor refines prayer times for Muslims from Jan 1
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Nov 25 — Selangor will set prayer times by nine districts instead of three zones from January 1, ahead of Ramadan next year, to make worship timings more accurate for Muslims in the state, Harian Metro reported today.
Selangor Mufti Datuk Anhar Opir said the change was prompted partly by complaints and checks showing the Maghrib azan was inconsistent throughout Ramadan, which raised concerns about the validity of Muslims’ fasts.
“Residents in the east no longer need to wait four or even six minutes compared with the previous zone timing,” he was quoted as saying at a briefing on the change here.
He said the move bases prayer times on each district’s actual geographic position and narrows the gaps between areas.
The Muslim fasting month of Ramadan 2027 is expected to begin around February 8, subject to the moon sighting, which in Malaysia is confirmed by the Keeper of the Rulers’ Seal.
The nine districts are Sabak Bernam, Kuala Selangor, Hulu Selangor, Gombak, Petaling, Klang, Kuala Langat, Hulu Langat and Sepang.
Anhar said the old zones lumped districts together, with the first covering five districts and the second and third two each.
He said one reason for the change was complaints, and later checks, showing that the Maghrib azan was not consistent throughout Ramadan, raising concerns about the validity of Muslims’ fasts.
“There are many factors, but the first is that many Maghrib azan in early Ramadan came before the time, and our reports show it was four, three, even two minutes early,” he said.
Anhar said the data showed this happened every year, and that after verification, some calls came after the prayer time and so did not invalidate the fast, while others were indeed made before the time had set in at the location concerned.
He said Muslims need not worry about the change and should refer to the Selangor Mufti Department’s official website for their district’s timetable from January 1.
“We have already prepared the timetable for the nine districts from January to December next year, and it can be accessed and downloaded,” he said.
Anhar added that the department is in talks to include district-based Selangor prayer times in the Department of Islamic Development Malaysia’s Iman app, and will step up efforts to explain the change to every community in the state.

Title: Malaysia condemns Israeli strikes in Gaza that killed UNRWA staff member, injured three others
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 25 — Malaysia has strongly condemned the Zionist Israel regime’s strikes in Gaza on November 23 that killed a staff member of the United Nations Relief and Works Agency for Palestine Refugees in the Near East (UNRWA) and injured three others.
The Foreign Ministry said in a statement today that Israel’s continuing indiscriminate attacks targeting civilians and UN personnel constituted a blatant violation of international law, including the United Nations Charter.
“Malaysia calls on the international community to end Israel’s impunity and protect civilians, humanitarian aid workers and United Nations personnel,” the statement read.
Anadolu Ajansi reported on November 24 that one UNRWA staff member was killed and three others were injured in an Israeli attack in the Gaza Strip.
According to reports, a total of 397 UNRWA staff members and others supporting the agency’s work had been killed since Israel’s war on Gaza began in October 2023. — Bernama

Title: Heavy rain and lightning expected in parts of Perak and East Malaysia until 5pm
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 25 — The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has issued an afternoon thunderstorm advisory for parts of Perak, Sabah, Sarawak, and the Federal Territory of Labuan, warning of heavy downpours, lightning, and gusty winds until 5.00pm today.
The weather alert, released at 2.50pm, covers five central and northern districts in Perak: Hulu Perak, Kuala Kangsar, Kinta, Kampar, and Batang Padang, alerting road users to potential travel disruptions ahead of the evening commute.
Across East Malaysia, the advisory blankets widespread southern, coastal, and interior localities in Sarawak, including Kuching, Serian, Sri Aman, and Limbang. The warning concurrently extends across Gedong and Simunjan in the Samarahan division, alongside Song and Kapit in the Kapit division.
In Sabah, stormy conditions are forecast across the Interior division, spanning Sipitang, Kuala Penyu, Beaufort, and Membakut, as well as the populous West Coast corridor covering Papar, Penampang, Putatan, Kota Kinabalu, Tuaran, and Kota Belud. The bulletin also includes Tawau, Kudat, and the Sandakan division (specifically Kinabatangan and Sandakan), alongside the offshore Federal Territory of Labuan.
MetMalaysia issues thunderstorm warnings when satellite and radar indicators track rainfall intensity exceeding 20 millimetres per hour that is either imminent or expected to persist beyond an hour.
The department emphasised that these bulletins serve as short-term alerts with a maximum validity of six hours from the time of issuance, advising motorists and residents across the affected zones to exercise caution and take precautions against localised flash floods, sudden wind squalls, and falling trees.

Title: Marine police seize RM5.36m worth of syabu after 90-minute high-speed boat chase off Kedah
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Nov 25 — The Region 1 Marine Police Force (PPM) has crippled a transnational drug smuggling syndicate operating through sea routes following the seizure of over 103 kilogrammes (kg) of syabu (methamphetamine) worth RM5.36 million and the arrest of four men in operations in the waters off Tanjung Dawai and Sungai Petani, Kedah, recently.
Bukit Aman Internal Security and Public Order Department (KDNKA) director Datuk Seri Mohd Yusri Hassan Basri said the team conducting patrol at 9pm on November 14 detected a suspicious fibreglass boat about seven nautical miles from Pulau Sayak in the waters off Tanjung Dawai.
“When instructed to stop for inspection, the boat sped off and made several dangerous manoeuvres in a bid to evade capture.
“However, our team managed to intercept the boat after a 90-minute high-speed chase, and we arrested two Indonesian men who were on board,” he told a press conference at the Region One PPM Headquarters here today, which was also attended by Bukit Aman PPM commander SAC Shamsol Kassim.
Mohd Yusri said an inspection of the boat lead to the discovery of five white sacks containing 100 gold-coloured plastic packets labelled “VIP 666” filled with 103kg of syabu estimated to be worth RM5.36 million, which were concealed in a specially constructed compartment in the boat.
Following the arrests, he said police raided a house in Kampung Sungai Layar Hujung, Sungai Petani and detained two more men - a Malaysian and an Indonesian - on November 15.
“The 36-year-old Malaysian suspect, who is self-employed and runs a grocery shop, is believed to be the mastermind behind the drug trafficking syndicate, planning and coordinating the drug shipments, as well as offering RM12,000 for each trip to transport the drugs to Indonesia.
“Further investigations found that the two men arrested were believed to have made six trips to smuggle drugs from Malaysia to a neighbouring country via sea routes to avoid detection by the authorities,” he added.
Mohd Yusri said although the three Indonesian suspects had valid passports, they were believed to have entered the country through unofficial entry points to carry out the drug smuggling activities.
Police also seized the fibreglass boat and a Toyota Hilux four-wheel drive vehicle, while the seized drugs could feed the habit of 518,990 addicts.
He said further investigations are ongoing, including efforts to trace the syndicate’s distribution network, while all four suspects, aged between 31 and 36, are being investigated under Section 39B of the Dangerous Drugs Act 1952.
The operation involved one officer and 18 personnel from the Region One PPM, with support from the Marine Intelligence Unit and patrol boats PSC 45, PSC 60 and PIB 01.
Meanwhile, Mohd Yusri said Region One PPM recorded 151 drug-related cases from January to November this year, resulting in 180 arrests and seizures of illicit substances worth RM11.96 million.
In total, 2,375 cases were recorded, with 1,462 arrests and seizures, including forfeitures, valued at RM187.99 million. — Bernama

Title: Bukit Aman warns drug syndicates may target other airports amid tighter KLIA security
Article:
TUMPAT, Nov 25 — Drug smuggling syndicates could target Sultan Ismail Petra Airport in Kota Bharu following attempts to use other airports since security was tightened at Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA), Bukit Aman said.
Bukit Aman Narcotics Criminal Investigation Department director Datuk Hussein Omar Khan said the syndicates were constantly looking for alternative routes to smuggle drugs.
“When we tightened security at KLIA, there were attempts to use the airports in Penang and Ipoh. We believe these syndicates will target other airports too,” he said.
He told reporters this after a welfare visit and the presentation of a mock cheque under the Royal Malaysia Police Cooperative’s group insurance scheme in Kampung Tengah Geting, Pengkalan Kubor, here today.
He said the attempts showed that the syndicates would seize any opportunity to evade tighter security at KLIA, thus he called for tighter security at all airports nationwide.
Hussein said the Home Ministry had already taken steps to strengthen security at all airports and would introduce further measures over the short, medium and long term.
He said the measures were needed to prevent syndicates from exploiting security gaps or shifting their operations elsewhere when the authorities tightened controls on a particular route.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim was previously reported as saying that the government should extend the use of closed-circuit television (CCTV) cameras with artificial intelligence (AI) analytics to detect drug smuggling at other airports. — Bernama

Title: Govt considers naming KL street after A. Samad Said, setting up gallery to honour his legacy
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 25 — The government will consider naming a Kuala Lumpur street after the late National Laureate Datuk Seri A Samad Said and setting up a gallery to showcase his work, Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said today.
Fahmi said veteran journalist Datuk A. Kadir Jasin proposed naming the street in recognition of Samad’s contributions to literature and journalism.
“We will look at these proposals, God willing. For me, what matters most is that we appreciate his work and remember that he championed the rights of ordinary people,” he told reporters at Masjid Saidina Abu Bakar As-Siddiq in Bangsar.
Fahmi said a gallery was also worth considering as a way to honour Samad and introduce his writing to younger readers.
“His works are still popular, but we need to introduce them to younger generations, particularly Gen Z and Gen Alpha,” he said.
Fahmi said he had also spoken to one of Samad’s children about copyright and how the family could preserve his writing.
The national laureate, fondly known as Pak Samad, died at 6.10pm yesterday after receiving treatment at Hospital Kuala Lumpur for diabetes and age-related illness.
Hundreds of mourners, including relatives, fellow artists and members of the public, attended funeral prayers at the mosque, led by imam Muhammad Abid Ayub.
Among those present were Chief Secretary to the Government Tan Sri Shamsul Azri Abu Bakar, Kadir and singer-composer Datuk M. Nasir.
Samad was later laid to rest at Bukit Kiara Muslim Cemetery. — Bernama

Title: Malaysia benefits immensely as a trading nation by engaging with world leaders, says Anwar
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 25 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said Malaysia has benefited immensely as a trading nation, and this is reflected in its engagements with world leaders, particularly during the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Economic Leaders’ Meeting held recently in Shenzhen, China.
Anwar, who is also the Finance Minister, said he met with US President Donald Trump during the Asean-US Special Summit in Manila, which was held in conjunction with the 49th Asean Summit, as well as Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin in Shenzhen.
“This way, I think only Malaysia has the capacity to focus on its own interests and to conduct its affairs based on our own foreign policy, respecting democratic trade relations and the policy of centrality.
“In the past, maybe it may have been quite controversial and even contentious when you meet President Putin. So I was quite relieved when President Xi Jinping, President Trump and President Putin sat down together. It gives us space to manoeuvre and seek ways to benefit our country,” he said in his speech at the document exchange ceremony for Malaysia Aviation Group’s long-range widebody aircraft acquisition.
In Shenzhen, the three world leaders held their first-ever trilateral summit on the sidelines of the APEC Economic Leaders’ Meeting.
“As Malaysia is a trading nation, we have benefited immensely through open trade, investment and international partnership,” he said.
He also said the US remains an important trading and investment partner, and the presence of Boeing as a partner reflects its confidence in Malaysia and Malaysia Aviation Group.
“And I believe this relationship will continue. For the industry, we will make sure that we cement this relationship in the interest of our people and our economy. And I would reiterate that as a trading nation, the need to engage with all countries is critical and pivotal to the economy. And I believe, InsyaAllah, we will do so,” he added.
Anwar noted that aviation was central to this success, serving as a critical enabler by strengthening Malaysia’s links to global markets and creating opportunities that benefit businesses, industries and communities across the country.
Earlier, Malaysia Aviation Group announced the acquisition of 10 Boeing 787 Dreamliner aircraft, with an option for six more, as part of its fleet modernisation strategy. — Bernama

Title: Court grants gag order in border agency chief Shuhaily’s case, media allowed to report proceedings
Article:
SEPANG, Nov 25 — The Magistrate’s Court today set December 23 for the remention of the case involving the director-general of the Malaysian Border Control and Protection Agency (AKPS), Datuk Seri Mohd Shuhaily Mohd Zain, who faces two charges of causing injury to police personnel.
Magistrate Khairatul Animah Jelani set the date for case management after the defence informed the court that they had received the relevant case documents from the prosecution this morning.
Earlier, the defence had requested that the case management be scheduled for January 20 next year to allow them time to review the documents.
However, Khairatul Animah said the case management must be set within 60 days from the date of the first mention.
During today’s proceedings, the court also granted the defence’s application for a restraining order against the parties involved in the case.
Meanwhile, lawyer Datuk Rosal Azimin Ahmad, representing Mohd Shuhaily, said the court had granted an application for a “gag order” against the parties involved in the case.
“This morning, the defence applied for a ‘gag order’ to prevent any party from making statements that are sub judice or prejudicial to any party with the exception of the media, who remain permitted to report on the court proceedings.
“This restraining order binds the defence, the prosecution, and watching-brief counsel, prohibiting them from issuing any statements that could compromise the trial until the case is concluded. This application was made to ensure our client receives a fair trial, and we hope all parties will respect the court’s decision,” he said when met by the media following the case mention proceedings today.
Earlier, Mohd Shuhaily arrived at the court at 8.20am for the mention of the case, in which he faces charges of causing injury to two police officers.
Dressed in a dark blue suit, Mohd Shuhaily was accompanied by the Port Klang district police chief (OCPD), Datuk Nik Ezanee Mohd Faisal.
On October 21, Mohd Shuhaily pleaded not guilty to two charges of intentionally causing injury to two police officers.
According to the charges, he allegedly caused injury to Mohammad Faiz Muhamad Saman, 40, and Muhammad Ekmal Sofwan Dirman, 25, near Counter J, Level 5, Terminal 1, Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA), between 1.27pm and 1.35pm on September 28.
Both charges were brought under Section 323 of the Penal Code, which carries a maximum penalty of one year in prison, a fine of up to RM2,000, or both, upon conviction.
The court had previously granted Mohd Shuhaily bail of RM3,000 for both charges, with one surety, and ordered him to be present for all subsequent trial proceedings.
The prosecution was handled by deputy public prosecutors Shahrizat Ismail, Datuk Ahmad Sazali Omar, Nor Azizah Aling, and Nur Aqiilah Ahmad Rofaie.
Mohd Shuhaily is represented by a legal team that includes Datuk Rosal Azimin Ahmad and Datuk Yaacob. Md Sam, Datuk Dr Baljit Singh Sidhu, Datuk Akberdin Abdul Kader, Datuk Ahmad Zaidi Zainal, Md Yunos Shariff, Muhammad Rafique Rashid Ali, and Kitson Foong. — Bernama

Title: Malaysians lost RM7.33b to online scams since 2023, Dewan Rakyat told
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 25 — Malaysians lost RM7.33 billion to online scams since 2023, Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail told the Dewan Rakyat today, warning that cyber fraud cases continue to climb with women and private sector employees bearing the brunt.
Between January 2023 and October 2026, the authorities recorded 192,869 online scam cases, resulting in 75,266 arrests and 69,665 charges brought to court, the home minister revealed.
The police logged 56,802 cases involving RM1.56 billion in losses for the first 10 months of this year alone, leading to 20,842 arrests and charges filed against 18,369 individuals across 17,985 investigation papers.
“This data allows us to draw only one conclusion: the trend of this crime is rising,” Saifuddin told the Lower House during Question Time.
Women outnumber men at a ratio of six to four, while private sector employees make up the largest occupational group targeted by fraudsters, the minister added.
Syndicates rely heavily on mule bank accounts to operate, with the authorities detecting 254,546 such accounts between 2023 and October this year, with 137,699 prosecuted so far.
Students make up a significant portion of those allowing their bank accounts to be used as mules, a trend Saifuddin described as “alarming”.
“These syndicates simply cannot operate without mule accounts,” he said.
Authorities have categorised online fraud into six primary modus operandi: telecommunications scams, e-financial crimes, love scams, e-commerce fraud, non-existent loans, and non-existent investment schemes.
By volume, telecommunications fraud topped the list with 73,043 cases involving RM2.132 billion in losses, followed by e-commerce scams with 50,749 cases totalling RM509 million.
But fake investment schemes proved to be the most financially devastating, accounting for RM3.4 billion in losses across 27,863 cases, or nearly half of the total amount lost since 2023.

Title: Malaysia must prepare for quantum computing and rogue AI threats, Fahmi says
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 25 — Malaysia must rapidly upgrade its national cybersecurity defences in lockstep with physical infrastructure investments to shield the country from emerging vulnerabilities posed by quantum computing and autonomous rogue agentic artificial intelligence, Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said today.
Addressing the opening of the NEXSEC2026 cybersecurity conference at the Malaysia International Trade and Exhibition Centre (MITEC), Fahmi said that the government is prioritising quantum migration and post-quantum cryptography to prevent sensitive data traversing domestic telecommunications networks from being compromised.
“This is why I have tasked the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) with convening research and development discussions on quantum migration and quantum-safe communications involving telecommunications companies and infrastructure providers.
“The shift towards quantum-safe communications is increasingly important to ensure data transmitted through telecommunications networks remains protected against interception, theft and hacking by cybercriminals,” he said.
Quantum migration involves upgrading legacy encryption protocols and security architecture to quantum-resistant algorithms capable of withstanding the unprecedented processing power of future quantum supercomputers.
For Malaysia, this transition requires retrofitting national telecommunication backbones and cloud routing systems to neutralize “harvest-now, decrypt-later” surveillance threats before quantum machines reach commercial maturity.
Fahmi warned that constructing world-class fibre and data centre infrastructure yields little value if sovereign data remains exposed to sophisticated digital intrusion.
However, he acknowledged that transitioning to quantum-safe communications entails substantial capital outlays, urging telecommunications operators and digital infrastructure concessionaires to strategically balance baseline capacity expansions with targeted cybersecurity expenditures.
The minister’s directive was delivered during NEXSEC2026, MCMC’s flagship cybersecurity symposium convened to assess sector readiness, accelerate advanced cyber engineering talent, and expand threat intelligence sharing among network operators, statutory agencies, and tertiary research institutions.

Title: Fresh blood for GPS: 11 new faces in 82-strong Sarawak election line-up
Article:
KUCHING, Nov 25 — Gabungan Parti Sarawak (GPS) is fielding 11 new faces among the 82 candidates announced by its chairman Tan Sri Abang Johari Openg for the 13th Sarawak state election.
The revamped line-up, announced at Parti Pesaka Bumiputera Bersatu (PBB) headquarters here, also features five women candidates, reflecting the coalition’s continued efforts to ensure female representation in the state’s political leadership.
The new faces are Wong Duk Ying (Padungan), Dayang Nurfizawati Abang Abdul Karim (Muara Tuang), Yussuf Chik (Simunjan), Awang Nashfarini Awang Sarbini (Beting Maro), Leonard Libau Anol (Simanggang), Nor-E-Fadzwie Salleh (Kabong), Alexander Donald (Ngemah), Kevin Lau Kor Jie (Bawang Assan), Cerisologo Sabut (Pelagus), Nur Fatin Syafawani Tahamat (Bekenu) and Datu Jack Liam (Batu Danau).
Several of the new candidates will be taking over from seasoned incumbents including Bawang Assan, where Datuk Seri Wong Soon Koh is stepping aside after seven terms, as well as Simanggang and Bekenu, previously represented by Datuk Francis Harden Hollis and Datuk Rosey Yunus, who had served six and four terms respectively.
Abang Johari, who is caretaker premier, said the 11 new faces accounted for 14 per cent of the coalition’s total line-up.
“The average age of the new candidates is approximately between 40 and 50 years old,” he told a press conference at the PBB headquarters here.
He said the new line-up reflected GPS’ decision to give more opportunities to incoming leaders and broaden participation within its component parties.
“I would like to thank those who have served as GPS representatives in the previous term. I also thank those who have decided to step aside and give new faces an opportunity.
“This is part of our process of rejuvenating GPS and its respective component parties,” he said.
Abang Johari said the new GPS candidate line-up also sees an increase in women’s representation, with five female candidates being fielded compared to four in the previous state election.
They are Datuk Seri Fatimah Abdullah (Dalat), Datuk Sharifah Hasidah Sayeed Aman Ghazali (Samariang), Dayang Noorazah Awang Sohor (Lingga), as well as the two new faces, Nur Fatin Syafawani and Dayang Nurfizawati.
“We have also included more youths or young candidates which shows that we are recognising the capabilities of young people in the coming election.
“In fact, all the component parties have fielded young candidates. For example, our candidate contesting in Beting Maro is only 35 years old,” he said.
The candidate announcement also saw several significant changes in seat representation, particularly involving the Sarawak United People’s Party (SUPP), which will field 18 candidates, including incumbents See Chee How and Dr Johnichal Rayong Ngipa in Batu Lintang and Engkilili respectively.
Both constituencies are traditionally SUPP seats, although they were won by Parti Sarawak Bersatu (PSB) candidates in the 2021 state election.
See won Batu Lintang under the PSB ticket in 2021 and subsequently served as an independent assemblyman after leaving the party in 2022, while Rayong won Engkilili under PSB before joining the Progressive Democratic Party (PDP) in 2024 following PSB’s dissolution.
Rayong recently resigned from PDP, effective November 22, alongside Soon Koh, with both maintaining their support for GPS and Abang Johari’s leadership.
For Bawang Assan, GPS has fielded Lau under the SUPP ticket, while PDP president Datuk Seri Tiong King Sing will defend Dudong.
In terms of the overall seat distribution, PBB remains the largest component party with 47 candidates, followed by SUPP with 18, Parti Rakyat Sarawak with 11 and PDP with six.
The line-up maintains the same overall distribution as the original GPS seat allocation in the 2021 election, although the political circumstances surrounding several constituencies have since changed.
Abang Johari also expressed appreciation to parties which will not be contesting against GPS this state election, particularly its partners in the federal unity government, namely Barisan Nasional, Parti Amanah Negara and PKR.
